The wait is almost over for fans of The Celebrity Traitors, with the BBC confirming that the adored show will return to screens in just a matter of weeks.

Claudia Winkleman, fringed and clad in tartan and wool, will be back to host the smash-hit show’s second season on Thursday 1 October at 8pm.

The multi-award-winning game of deception will air two nights a week on Thursday and Friday evenings at 8pm.

A new trailer shows the celebrity players meet each other and take part in an explosive mission. Joining Winkleman in the Scottish Highlands this year are Amol Rajan, Bella Ramsey, James Acaster, James Blunt, Jerry Hall, Joanne McNally, Joe Lycett, Julie Hesmondhalgh, King Kenny, Leigh-Anne Pinnock, Maya Jama, Michael Sheen, Miranda Hart, Myha’la, Professor Hannah Fry, Richard E Grant, Rob Beckett, Romesh Ranganathan, Ross Kemp, Sebastian Croft and Sharon Rooney.

They will compete to win a prize of £100,000 for a charity of their choice.

“If this is the last time we’re friends, good luck,” Jama can be heard telling her fellow players in one of the classic Traitors jeeps.

“My heart is racing,” Ramsey, the star of The Last of Us, can be heard admitting at another point, while Ranganathan and Beckett are seen confronting each other over whether they are Traitors.

The official video podcast, The Celebrity Traitors: Uncloaked, will also return to BBC One, BBC iPlayer and BBC Sounds with host Ed Gamble.

Series one of The Celebrity Traitors debuted on BBC One in October 2025 and was a runaway success, averaging 14.9 million viewers across the run with a peak of 15.4 million for the finale, which saw a giggling Alan Carr win the prize pot as an undetected Traitor.

According to Ed Havard, the BBC’s director of entertainment, the new series of Celebrity Traitors will see the stakes upped from its inaugural hit season last year, and will feature “tears” and “paranoia that’s off the scale”.

“The thing about this season is things happen that you didn't think could happen on Traitors, that you have never seen before,” he said, during an appearance at the Edinburgh TV Festival.

Celebrity Traitors’ initial series featured a starry lineup including actors Celia Imrie and Nick Mohammed, musician Paloma Faith, author and actor Stephen Fry, presenter Jonathan Ross, and comedian Carr.

The classic, non-celebrity edition of the show is expected to return in January 2027.

Progressive U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon, a close ally of President Donald Trump, called for new restrictions on artificial intelligence systems Tuesday, forming an unexpected alliance around shared fears that the technology poses a threat to human safety.

Appearing at the same event in Washington, both figures warned of potentially catastrophic fallout for humanity, reflecting how concerns over AI risks are expanding well beyond Silicon Valley and traditional political channels.

Sanders, a democratic socialist, spoke first to warn of the "growing threat" posed by the technology and argued that mandatory safety regulations are essential to rein in the industry.

"AI has the potential to eliminate tens of millions of jobs, wiping out entire professions and making it harder for our young people to enter the workforce,” he said. "As many scientists believe could happen, this technology will escape human control with potentially catastrophic consequences."

open image in gallery Bernie Sanders called on Trump to negotiate a treaty with Chinese President Xi Jinping at their summit next week to pause AI development ( Reuters )

The senator drew applause from attendees when he criticized technology executives for concentrating control over AI developments, pointing specifically to SpaceX CEO and former Trump adviser Elon Musk.

“This week, as all of you know, Dario Amodei, Elon Musk and Sam Altman, leaders of major American AI companies, all agreed we must slow the development of AI and ‘pace the frontier,’” Sanders said. “That is a start but it’s not enough. When you’re racing towards a cliff, you don’t just ease up on the gas pedal. You hit the brakes.”

He continued, “When the future of humanity is at stake, we need binding international safety rules, not voluntary industry standards from the industry.”

Sanders urged Trump to negotiate a treaty with Chinese President Xi Jinping during their summit next week to enact a temporary pause on AI advancement.

"Last month, we learned that AI has been used for the first time ever to create new viruses. In the wrong hands, this could lead to new bioweapons and a potential global pandemic that could lead to the deaths of tens of millions of people," Sanders said.

Steve Bannon calls for executive action

Bannon, who served as a White House strategist during Trump's first presidential term, has openly questioned Trump's approach to overseeing the industry, attributing the president's unwillingness to regulate the technology to the influence of tech corporations. On his podcast on Monday, Bannon argued that Congress should refrain from passing laws that block individual states from establishing their own regulatory standards.

Speaking on Tuesday, Bannon characterized AI as the defining issue of the modern era.

"Here's what we have to do first: to slow down the pace so that we can understand exactly what's going on," Bannon said. He praised Sanders' summary of the risks involved and urged politicians to transcend party lines on the matter.

"I don't think you could find any too harder partisans than Bernie Sanders on the left and Steve Bannon on the right," he noted.

open image in gallery Steve Bannon, who served as a White House strategist during Trump's first presidential term, has openly questioned Trump's approach to overseeing the industry ( Reuters )

Bannon maintained that congressional action would prove too slow to effectively manage the pace of development. "This is going to have to be executive action," Bannon said, while also arguing that the U.S. must completely cut off China from American-made computer chips.

The shared platform between Sanders and Bannon, who occupy opposing ends of the political spectrum, highlights how anxieties over AI and its infrastructure are forging unusual political alliances.

Trump downplays AI concerns

Trump, however, downplayed such concerns on Monday following warnings from industry leaders over the weekend regarding potential misuse, insisting that the U.S. already possesses sufficient guardrails.

Echoing Trump's stance, Republican U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Tuesday that a moratorium on development would cause the nation to lose its competitive edge against China, maintaining that AI firms are capable of managing themselves.

"They can self-regulate. They don't need the government to tell them to slow it down. If they want to slow it down, they should," Johnson told reporters. That view is shared by industry figures including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who argue that government oversight would hamper U.S. competitiveness.

Recent public opinion polls indicate that a majority of Americans remain concerned that AI could eliminate jobs, inflate household expenses, or trigger wider social harms.

As the U.S. House of Representatives returned from its summer recess on Monday, lawmakers in both chambers held private discussions regarding potential AI legislation, even after Trump asserted that legislative intervention was unnecessary.

Congress has faced past criticism for lacking the technical expertise needed to effectively regulate tech companies. Commenting on the legislative hurdles, Republican Senator Bernie Moreno of Ohio said, "This process of legislating takes so long. Imagine AI four years in. We're dealing with stuff that isn't even relevant in four years."

Public resistance is also building against proposed data centers required for the AI expansion, with a June Reuters/Ipsos poll showing 77% of Americans worry these facilities will drive up electricity costs.

Concerns have also surfaced from within the tech sector itself. Jacob Coxon, a researcher who recently departed Anthropic, attracted attention last week after stating he resigned partly because the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."

On Tuesday, Andrew Ferguson, the chairman of the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, voiced skepticism toward AI companies seeking antitrust exemptions while simultaneously lobbying for new regulatory frameworks. Meanwhile, U.S. senators continue to debate a bill that would prevent states from enforcing local rules on AI risks.

The Washington event also featured AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler, leader of the nation's largest labor union federation. Sanders, along with progressive Representative Greg Casar, has called for federal legislation to pause the development of AI tools capable of "overthrowing or undermining the U.S. government," pending the creation of a new oversight agency.

Sixty-three years ago, dynamite planted by Ku Klux Klan members exploded through the 16th Street Baptist Church in Birmingham, Alabama, killing four girls as they prepared for Sunday services.

Hundreds of people filled the church on Tuesday on the 63rd anniversary of the bombing. The church marked the anniversary with the opening of a new visitors center that leaders said is aimed at educating people about one of the most horrific events of the Civil Rights Movement and urging a recommitment to continue the struggle for justice.

Bryan Stevenson, the founder of the Equal Justice Initiative and the guest speaker for the annual memorial service, said the remembrance falls at a time when politicians are trying to take content out of museums, attacking the Voting Rights Act and turning to the politics of division.

“We’re in a critical moment in America. There is a narrative struggle. There are people who are preaching the politics of fear and anger, and they want to govern through fear and anger,” Stevenson said.

Stevenson, who helped build memorials and museums tracing the legacy of slavery in America, said a “whole network of elected officials" — not only the Klan — shared responsibility for the climate that led to the deadly bombing.

“And today we have those same voices, and we have to stand against those voices by being committed to truth and justice,” Stevenson said.

Klansmen had placed a bundle of dynamite outside the church under a set of stairs. The bombing came during the height of the Civil Rights Movement, eight months after then-Gov. George Wallace pledged “segregation forever.”

The girls were gathered in a downstairs washroom before Sunday services when the dynamite exploded at 10:22 a.m. on Sept. 15, 1963. The explosion killed 11-year-old Denise McNair and Cynthia Wesley, Carole Robertson and Addie Mae Collins, all 14. A fifth girl, Sarah Collins Rudolph, the sister of Addie Mae, was in the room and was severely injured but survived.

Three Ku Klux Klansmen were eventually convicted in the blast: Robert Chambliss in 1977; Thomas Blanton in 2001; and Bobby Frank Cherry in 2002.

The opening of the education center comes at a time of uncertainty about how history is presented in national parks and museums. President Donald Trump in March 2025 signed an executive order aimed at defunding museum exhibits and programs that he said promote “divisive narratives.”

The church sits within the bounds of the National Park Service's civil rights monument in Birmingham, an area that includes the park where Black protesters were met by police dogs and fire hoses. But the church independently runs the visitors center.

The new center has space for exhibits, oral history initiatives, artist residencies, community quilting projects, public speaker series and other programming.

Church leaders envision the center as a place where people can reflect after visiting the church and bombing site.

“I want them to take away that history is not just in the past. History is also present, and that there’s still work to do,” said the Rev. Arthur Price Jr., the pastor of 16th Street Baptist. “When we talk about the challenges in our country, when we talk about the injustice, the inequity, and the inequality, there’s still a whole lot of work for us to do.”

Lisa McNair’s sister, Denise, was one of the girls who lost their lives in the 1963 bombing.

“It’s part of our shared American history, and if we don’t know our history, we’re destined to repeat it,” McNair said at Tuesday's event.

Kelly Osbourne is opening up about one of the last conversations she had with her father, Ozzy Osbourne.

Days before the Black Sabbath frontman died at age 76 in July 2025, Kelly said in a new podcast appearance that Ozzy shared a message to remember after his death.

“He sat me down, this was about three days before he died,” Kelly, 41, said on Paul C. Brunson’s We Need to Talk podcast. “He sat me down and said, ‘Tots, I need you to know something. No matter what happens in this life, you can live the rest of your life knowing that there was one man on this planet that truly loved you. That truly loved you for every single thing you are. And that man is me.’”

Kelly said that she started to cry at the sentiment and begged him not to “talk like this,” which prompted him to respond, “You know, I’m not going to be here forever. And I know you struggle with people and believing you are loved. But I love you more than anyone.”

The Prince of Darkness died from a heart attack July 22, 2025, after years of health issues ranging from Parkinson’s disease to neck and back injuries. The rock legend died at his mansion in Welders, Buckinghamshire, and was surrounded by Sharon Osbourne, his wife of 43 years, and their three children: Aimee, Jack and Kelly.

open image in gallery Kelly Osbourne opened up about her father’s final message to her before his death ( YouTube: We Need to Talk )

open image in gallery British singer-songwriter Ozzy Osbourne and his daughter Kelly Osbourne ( AFP/Getty )

Elsewhere in Kelly’s podcast interview, the reality TV personality spoke about the struggles she dealt with after her father’s death.

“I was a shell of myself,” she said. “I couldn’t speak. I couldn’t eat. I couldn’t do anything. I was just empty.”

Kelly continued: “Broken in every way a human being could possibly be broken and completely unable to even take care of myself. I was at ground zero. I started drinking again. I lost my mind. I couldn’t handle it.”

The rockstar’s daughter went on to say that she “lost a lot of friends” as she grieved. “I closed my circle because I lost a lot of friends because people don’t like sadness and they expected me to be over it,” she said. “I will never be over it. I will never, ever be over it.”

Earlier this month, Kelly addressed concerns surrounding her weight loss after Ozzy’s death and said that she “couldn’t see what other people saw” because she was in pain. “All I saw was a broken person,” she said.

Four supporting acts have quit Ed Sheeran’s tour after rapper Macklemore was dropped over pro-Palestinian remarks he made on stage.

Hours after Sheeran said he would not be drawn into a public debate about the Gaza war, Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga, the Danish band Lukas Graham, and Finneas said on Instagram that they were withdrawing from the tour.

Rowe was one of Macklemore’s replacements for Sheeran’s remaining U.S. dates, while Beoga was serving as Sheeran’s touring band. Finneas, Billie Eilish’s brother and musical collaborator, was due to tour with Sheeran in South America later this year.

“Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed,” Finneas wrote. “I have decided to withdraw from my upcoming tour dates with Ed Sheeran. I stand with Palestine and its people.”

Aaron Rowe’s message read in part, “I don’t take the decision likely. Ed has been a friend to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this.”

open image in gallery Macklemore was scheduled for eight of Sheeran’s 10 remaining stadium shows, resuming Saturday in Philadelphia ( Getty )

Beoga said in part, “We have made the decision to depart as Ed Sheeran’s band on the remaining US Loop tour, following the silencing of Macklemore by zionist lobbies.”

Rowe and Beoga each cited their country’s history in their statements explaining their decision.

“We are Irish people who understand colonialism. As founding members of the Irish Artists for Palestine movement, we are committed activists for justice and will continue to be,” Beoga said.

Lukas Graham, meanwhile, expressed gratitude toward Sheeran and called it “a difficult decision.”

“Money doesn’t give you the right to own the conversation. Nobody’s bank balance should decide who gets to speak or which suffering we’re allowed to acknowledge,” the band posted, seemingly referring to billionaire Robert Kraft’s role in Macklemore’s removal from the tour.

Earlier Tuesday, Sheeran addressed Macklemore being removed as his opening act and shifted the blame to promoters.

"Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine," Sheeran said on Instagram. "I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living."

What Macklemore said on stage

Macklemore said Monday that he was removed from the Loop Tour after shouting "Free Palestine!" during a Sept. 5 performance at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey while performing his protest song Hind’s Hall.

Addressing the audience during the show, Macklemore said: "To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters, criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide, it in no way is criticism of you."

Macklemore said several U.S. venues notified the promoter that they would forbid him from appearing as Sheeran’s opener. The ban was led by NFL’s New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft. Kraft's company, Kraft Group, owns Gillette Stadium.

open image in gallery New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft was behind the push to remove Macklemore (pictured) ( Getty )

In a statement released Monday, Kraft said the decision to remove Macklemore followed his recent comments "and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community."

Sheeran wrote in his post that he "spoke with the venues at length all week to try to build a bridge," but acknowledged that "the venue's and promoter's decision was final."

A growing number of organizations and experts assert that Israel’s actions in Gaza constitute genocide, an allegation Israel firmly denies.

Macklemore was scheduled for eight of Sheeran’s 10 remaining stadium shows, resuming Saturday in Philadelphia with Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe billed. Upcoming stops include Gillette Stadium, Atlanta’s Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and Indianapolis’ Lucas Oil Stadium.

Sheeran said he aims to use music to bring diverse audiences together, adding that while he holds personal views on "this devastating conflict," he chooses not to speak publicly because concertgoers "do not expect a political forum." He added: "I am not complicit."

"I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes," Sheeran added. "However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace. I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed."

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit 19-year high as global bond rout intensifies
News.content:
The cost of UK government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007 in a fresh global debt sell-off.

The yield on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, rose from 5.37pc to a fresh 19-year high of 5.41pc on Tuesday as rising oil prices risk reigniting inflation.

Mortgage experts have warned that residential and buy-to-let mortgage rates are set to climb towards 5pc, as market turmoil threatens to filter through to household finances.

Short-term debt costs have also jumped, with the yield on two-year UK bonds surpassing 4.9pc for the first time in three years.

The bond chaos came as Andy Haldane, a former Bank of England chief economist, warned that Labour risked becoming “just a traditional tax and spend socialist government with better TikTok videos”.

He told LBC that John Healey’s original plan for a “low drama budget” had been “torpedoed” by higher borrowing costs and “events over the last couple of weeks”.

He said: “I think that [the bond market turmoil] will mean some hard choices next month at the Budget.”

“Few hard choices so far, but one is looming on the horizon, how any hole to the budget headroom is made good on. Is that a question of tax rises, or is it a question of taking the knife to public spending.”

Mr Haldane has been advising Labour since Andy Burnham took power.

It comes as the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England face pressure to raise interest rates this week to combat rising prices.

Anthony Brinkman, a portfolio manager at Principal Asset Management, said: “The recent gilt market movements seem to be intent on showing central banks they are out of time – the market is expecting action.”

Borrowing costs around the world are rising after a 20pc surge in oil prices so far this month.

Brent crude tipped above $109 a barrel this week after Houthi rebels in Yemen, considered a proxy for Iran’s forces, seized control of a key port in the Red Sea, threatening shipping.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Wednesday in the face of the inflation threat.

As a result, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds has surged above 5pc for the first time since 2007.

News.title: AI could transform global inequalities or ‘widen the gap’, warns Bill Gates
News.content:
“AI could be a great equaliser, or [it could] widen the gap”, says Mr Gates. “This is not a long-range prediction. It’s a present-tense choice”.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident. After all, the market is an extraordinary engine of innovation, but a terrible guarantor of equal opportunity.

“With AI, the gap could grow even faster … That is what makes this moment so urgent. Things are changing rapidly, and the window to shape who benefits from AI, and how soon, is short”.

The key issue holding back the deployment of AI in the developing world revolves around the availability of local data and, in turn, the ability for the technology to scale in environments very different from where it is currently being created.

An app that is trained on billions of hours of American English, will struggle at first with British English (see your spell check) but is next to useless if your local language is Swahili or Chichewa.

More profoundly, an AI tool that allows a farmer in Hampshire to control his combine harvester remotely, will offer little to a smallholder in South Sudan who works the land by hand and faces a completely different array of pests, weather conditions and costs.

The same is true for health. “A community health worker in Rwanda examining a baby with a fever faces different questions than a clinician in a well-resourced hospital - and the AI supporting her needs to reflect that”, says Mr Gates.

He adds: “Most of the world is invisible to today’s AI models. These AI systems were trained primarily on what exists on the internet – and the internet reflects a deeply unequal world. More than 90 percent of the data used to train early, large language models came from English-language sources. The communities that stand the most to gain from AI are largely absent from the knowledge base these tools are built on. They are not just underserved. They are not in the picture at all”.

The new investment aims to help correct that. Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation, says investments are already being made with companies including Microsoft and Google to build databases of a much wider range of languages, for instance.

Africa alone has more than 2,000 languages, and for AI’s to be effective there they have to understand what and how people actually speak - “their dialects, accents, and slang, too”.

The investments, he says, are being made on the condition that the intelligence and knowledge they accumulate are made freely available for others to use.

Languages for AI “are true public goods, almost definitional public goods. They need to be freely available to everybody. Once they’re created, they are public goods that can be uploaded onto any AI,” said Mr Suzman.

News.title: Reynolds refuses four times to rule out tax raid on state pensioners
News.content:
The Business Secretary refused four times to rule out retirees paying tax on the state pension from next year.

Jonathan Reynolds declined to reassure pensioners that they would not pay income tax on the benefit for the first time, saying it was a question for the Chancellor.

The comments on Tuesday raised concern for millions of retired people expecting to see their state pension surpass £13,000 from April, forcing them to pay income tax.

However, pensions minister Torsten Bell later insisted Labour would not put up taxes on people who rely on the state pension.

It is still unclear how this will be implemented given the complexity of separating the tax arrangements of different groups of pensioners.

The rise under the triple lock guarantee would drag many pensioners into paying income tax for the first time because their state income would surpass the personal allowance of £12,570.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, said last year that people solely reliant on the state pension would not have to pay the tax.

However, Mr Reynolds was repeatedly asked on BBC Breakfast whether Labour would honour this commitment after the next increase in the state pension in April. He declined to answer four times.

He said: “I’m sorry, that is for the Chancellor and for a Budget.

“The majority of pensioners in this country don’t just rely on the state pensions. Some do, I accept that, but the majority don’t.

“Sometimes when this is looked at, we’re focusing just on the state pension side of this. You’ve got to consider the full range of income retired people in the UK have.”

However Mr Bell, the pensions minister, walked back from Mr Reynolds comments.

He said: “In line with the commitment made at Budget 2025, pensioners who only just exceed the personal allowance will not have the administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax in this Parliament.

“The Chancellor will set out further details on how that commitment will be delivered at the Budget.”

Former pensions minister Sir Steve Webb said only one in 16 pensioners would benefit from this policy.

He said: “Those on the new state pension can expect to see an increase of nearly £500 per year next April.

“But the sting in the tail is that this will take the standard rate of the new state pension above the tax threshold.”

The comments came after official figures on Tuesday indicated the triple lock will rise by 3.9pc from April.

Under the triple lock, the state pension rises each April in line with inflation, average wages or 2.5pc, whichever is highest.

Total pay, including bonuses, rose by 3.9pc in the three months to July, down from 4.2pc in the three months to June.

Pensioners may yet receive a bigger increase if September’s inflation figure is higher than 3.9pc. That will be revealed next month but a higher figure is thought to be unlikely.

News.title: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon
News.content:
The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

News.title: Wall Street hit by tech sell-off after AI bosses push for slowdown
News.content:
Donald Trump has attacked what he calls a “sick conspiracy” against AI after the head of Anthropic called for a slowdown in the technology’s development.

The US president warned that China would benefit after the bosses of Silicon Valley’s top AI companies backed calls to restrict AI development for safety reasons, calling the concerns a “hoax”.

He also launched a tirade against Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, whom he accused of trying to be a “perfect little angel”.

Mr Trump wrote on Truth Social: “The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’ like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’ – and we will continue to do so!

“We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies!

“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China.”

Mr Amodei released a letter at the weekend calling for an industry-wide slowdown, endorsed by the US government, to prevent safety issues going “seriously wrong”.

In response, Mr Trump wrote: “Concerning AI, when, in the history of business, did anyone see the leaders of an industry call for regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy.

“AI taking over the world, destroying humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX.”

JD Vance, the US vice-president, echoed Mr Trump’s comments, calling tech leaders’ requests a “Trojan horse”.

He added: “I have to say, just personally, I feel a little bit weird about the fact that you have so many frontier AI tech companies kind of coming to the government and begging the government to regulate them.

“It feels a little bit to me like a bit of a Trojan horse.”

OpenAI has since called on the UK Government to introduce mandatory safety rules for major AI developers.

Under proposals supported by the company, the UK’s AI Security Institute would play a central role in third-party testing and creating adaptive technical standards.

Tom Duff-Gordon, the company’s head of policy in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, told Politico: “OpenAI is in a position to support legislation in the UK to establish durable, mandatory, capability-based requirements for frontier AI that would build on the set of voluntary commitments that we currently have.”

Under the plans, Britain would move from the current system of voluntary agreements with AI companies to enforceable standards, bringing the UK in line with emerging frameworks in the EU and US.

The Government has not yet put forward plans for AI safety legislation, despite pressure from backbench MPs.

US tech stocks fell sharply on Wall Street after AI bosses called for a slowdown, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping by as much as 1.3pc.

Nvidia, the world’s largest listed company and a manufacturer of semiconductors used in the AI race, plunged by 4.2pc while fellow chipmaker AMD dropped 6.2pc.

The main European indexes in France, Germany and Spain were all down sharply on Monday after falls in South Korea and Japan overnight.

News.title: The best boutique hotels in Madrid
News.content:
In Madrid, choosing a boutique hotel gives you the chance to stay in some of the Spanish capital’s most elegant buildings, with smart design and often palatial levels of grandeur. This is a particularly noisy and frantic city, but as soon as you step inside these calm havens, you can relax and get yourself ready for more urban adventures. The people on reception and behind the bar have more time to chat and are usually more than willing to spill their secrets on favourite bars, restaurants and shops.

Although these places are smaller than the chain hotels, they often have spectacular roof terraces as well as attractive spas and great restaurants. This is also an opportunity to stay in some of the smartest neighbourhoods, such as Salesas and Salamanca, where you might find yourself fantasising about living in Madrid as you drift around the boutiques and bakeries near your hotel. News.title: 50 of the most family-friendly hotels in France
News.content:
La belle France promises endless family escapades – by the sea or sand dunes, overlooking horse-ploughed vines or atop a mountain or a clifftop. Natural green space for children of all ages to let off steam is in abundance pretty much all over the hexagon, and as French hoteliers refine their services and facilities to make stays more eco-conscious, there’s never been a greener and more exhilarating choice of places to stay en famille. Château, chalet, hôtel particular (historic mansion), upcycled oil mill or belle epoque seaside villa: all budgets are embraced with signature French panache.

Sophisticated city hotels and resorts entertain with action-packed kids’ clubs, themed treasure hunts, outdoor activities and hands-on workshops like patisserie classes, grape-picking and cheese-making. Mid-range hotels pamper young explorers with traditional games, kitchen-garden visits and old-fashioned fun en plein air. Away from towns and cities, hotels increasingly offer flexible self-catering packages too – a cottage positioned on a rambling estate perhaps – allowing families to mix-and-match hotel dining with their own, memorable market-sourced feasts.

Located in Paris, Provence or pinprick hamlets you’ve probably never heard of: here are 50 of the best family-friendly hotels in France.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel quit threat is a blow to Man Utd but NOT a seismic setback for Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel quit threat is a blow to Man Utd but NOT a seismic setback for Michael Carrick

The prodigiously talented 15-year-old has shocked the club by asking for his Old Trafford agreement to be cancelled but his request is not overly unusual and will happen more often

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel has asked for his Manchester United registration to be cancelled

The talk about JJ Gabriel’s prodigious talent has been loud for a long time and everything he has done in Manchester United’s youth ranks has suggested the hype could well be justified. Which is why the news he wants to leave United has caused quite a stir.

‌



For every well-publicised prodigy that actually goes on to enjoy a successful professional career at an elite level, there is a well-publicised prodigy who does not make it at an elite level. Always remember that.

‌



A scarily good 15-year-old does not necessarily turn into a scarily good 25-year-old. Freddy Adu was billed as the next Pele when playing in Major League Soccer at the age of 15. At the age of 25, he was having an unsuccessful trial at Blackpool.

‌



But in the case of Gabriel’s future, it is hard to find anyone with any serious doubt over whether he will make it or not. He is, by common consent, the brightest prospect in the land.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He is an even brighter prospect, some say, than Max Dowman, who made his Premier League debut for Arsenal at 15 years and 235 days old. So, yes, it will be a blow for United if he does walk away, which certainly seems to be his intention.

The competition for marquee youngsters is intense. Rio Ngumoha was one of the most talked-about academy players in the Premier League but left Chelsea for Liverpool around his 16th birthday.

Gabriel turns 16 in three weeks’ time. Youngsters moving between powerhouse clubs is nothing new.

‌



View 3 Images JJ Gabriel was the youngest winner of the Manchester United Academy Player of the Year award (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Cesc Fabregas was a jewel of Barcelona’s fabled academy, La Masia, but walked away when he was 16 and joined Arsenal. It happens.

That is not to say Gabriel’s request will not concern United and their fans. This is Manchester United we are talking about. It should be a club that is the ultimate dream for any young player.

‌



But times have changed. For Gabriel’s generation - and probably his family’s generation - United is just another big club. They have not won a Premier League in 13 years and have not won a Champions League in 18 years.

Gabriel might look at Marcus Rashford - a predecessor as a prodigy - and wonder why the England attacker would have preferred to be at Barcelona this season. The reasons behind the decision of Gabriel and his family and his advisers are not yet crystal clear.

View 3 Images Rio Ngumoha left Chelsea for Liverpool at the age of 16 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



There is a suggestion that they thought he should be in United’s Champions League squad, in the same way Dowman was in Arsenal’s at a similar age. Whatever the reasons, they should be respected.

But it should be remembered that the old mantra about no one player being bigger than the club is still true. And especially when that player is not yet 16 years old and especially when that club is Manchester United.

Yes, it will be extremely annoying for United’s coaching staff, executives, and, indeed, fans. But of the issues Michael Carrick and the rest of those in charge of the footballing operation have, it is not a seismic setback.

Sports.title: Howard Webb points blame for Manchester derby offside controversy as Pro Ref take action
Sports.content:
Refereeing chief Howard Webb has claimed that VAR officials in Stockley Park had 'tunnel vision' before the decision to allow Erling Haaland's controversial winner in the Manchester derby.

Video assistant referee Matt Donohue and his assistant, Blake Antrobus, have both been stood down for this weekend's Premier League fixtures after wrongly letting Haaland's goal stand.

Initially flagged for offside due to Enzo Fernandez's attempt to play the ball in build-up, the decision was overturned following VAR check. Webb, as head of Pro Ref, wrote to Manchester United officials within hours of full-time to apologise for the error that played a decisive part in their 1-0 defeat to leave Michael Carrick's side on four points after four games.

Haaland's goal wasn't the only moment of drama at Old Trafford either. City star Phil Foden was sent off after kicking out at United captain Bruno Fernandes, a decision which Webb insists was correct.

‌



Appearing on Match Officials Mic'd Up, the former referee admitted: "We felt it was important that we acknowledged an error in this situation. We know that Erling Haaland, who was penalised on field for offside, wasn't in an offside position.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"But we also know that Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, almost certainly interfered with the Manchester United defence and probably the goalkeeper as well.

‌



"I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are. None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They'll not be officiating again until after the international break. We've reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen.

"They don't happen that often, but we want to ensure that we are transparent and open, and we've played the audio and the footage to the football club to let them know what happened, and we're going to review this situation to understand what elements of process fell down in this situation which meant we didn't get to the right outcome."

Should Phil Foden have been sent off? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez dived for the ball from an offside position (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Webb added that the officials back in Stockley Park got 'tunnel vision' in focusing on Haaland's part in the goal, with colleagues unable to pull him back out to look at the wider picture.

He added: "And when the VAR starts their check, they see through the use of the semi-automated offside technology, that Haaland, when he's played, is actually onside by three centimetres, played on by [Patrick] Dorgu on the far side, and the VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he's onside, he thinks that's a good goal, Haaland's not offside, as was thought initially.

"But of course, when he then runs it back through the full APP, he doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez's position. He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score. He doesn't touch the ball, but he doesn't truly evaluate other elements of offside. In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. He gets focused on Haaland, and it's down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn't happen on this occasion."

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez's role was incorrectly overlooked in the process of allowing the goal, according to Webb

‌



Webb then emphasised: "We'll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again."

City took the lead in the derby after they were reduced to 10 men. Tempers flared in the 23rd minute, as Foden reacted to a kick from Fernandes by lashing out himself.

On-field referee Michael Oliver quickly made up his mind and it was the City player who was punished. "I agree with the red card for Phil Foden for violent conduct," Webb concurred. "He kicks out with force into the upper body of Bruno Fernandes.

"We saw a player sent off for Aston Villa earlier in the season. [Joao] Gomes was sent off for a very similar thing, kicking with the studs into the body. And that's seen by the referee on the field, and that's the on-field call, a red card for Foden.

‌



"Now, when you look at the footage, there is that petulant kick by Bruno Fernandes into the backside of Foden. It is more petulant than violent.

"To be violent conduct, it has to have excessive force or brutality, and when you look at that, particularly in full speed, it doesn't have those elements. So therefore, this would be a yellow card offence. And the VAR can't step in to recommend the referee looks at the screen to give a yellow card.

"Of course, if all of this is missed and nothing is given against Foden, then the VAR could step in so the referee could see Foden's actions for a possible red card, and they would capture Fernandes' yellow card action. But because the referee gave the red card on the field, that option is not open to the VAR."

‌

Sports.title: Dominic Calvert-Lewin is thriving at Leeds while England rivals score cheap goals in Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is thriving at Leeds while England rivals score cheap goals in Saudi Arabia

The Leeds United striker has been on top form since his move from Everton and is line for an international recall when Thomas Tuchel names his latest squad

View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds United celebrates his goal to make it 3-0 vs Newcastle

Dominic Calvert-Lewin spent nine seasons in the Premier League with Everton and his most productive campaign was 2020/21 when he scored 16 goals in 33 appearances. He also scored twice in the FA Cup and three times in the EFL Cup.

‌



It was the full Covid season, played almost entirely behind closed doors. There was a theory amongst some Evertonians that Calvert-Lewin felt less pressure without the presence of a set of fans who could be highly critical.

‌



That theory seemed ill-founded. He played in nine matches behind closed doors in the restarted 2019/20 season and did not score once.

‌



And he has performed well under pressure many times in his career. But there is no doubt Calvert-Lewin can experience confidence swings.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



And he has spoken honestly and commendably about mental struggles during a career frequently interrupted by injury. Which is why it is fantastic to see Calvert-Lewin full of confidence, loving his football and looking in the form of his life.

He has now scored 16 goals in 34 Premier League appearances for Leeds United. Considering their serious striking issues - Thierno Barry being the only recognised centre-forward - some Everton fans have been lamenting that Calvert-Lewin was allowed to leave on a free transfer at the end of the 2024/25 season.

But realistically, the long-standing relationship - he was at Everton for nine seasons - had run its course and a change of scenery was best for him. And when he went to Elland Road, it was hard not to feel it would go one of two ways.

‌



View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin's last appearance for England was in a friendly against Uruguay in March (Image: Getty Images)

It would be confirmation that physical setbacks had taken a long-term toll on a hugely talented player or it would restart a career that has seemed so promising. It is most definitely the latter.

Calvert-Lewin turns 30 next March but there is every chance we have not seen the best of the Sheffield-born striker. It goes without saying that is fantastic news for Leeds United - it should also be fantastic news for England.

‌



Calvert-Lewin was unlucky not to be taken to the World Cup and Thomas Tuchel, who did give him half an hour in a friendly against Uruguay early in the year, will surely include him in his next squad, which will be announced on Friday. England have four UEFA Nations League matches coming up. They host world champions Spain before travelling to the Czech Republic and Croatia and then returning to Wembley to play the Czechs again.

The Leeds forward - rightly dismayed at having a goal taken away from him after his towering header took a nick off Jayden Bogle - will surely feature in parts of those games. Calvert-Lewin has just run amok against Newcastle in the Premier League, while Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney are content with cheap goals and bumper pay deals in Saudi Arabia.

View 3 Images England are still heavily reliant on captain Harry Kane (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Tuchel’s and England’s reliance on Harry Kane remains. And will do up until and throughout Euro 2028.

But Calvert-Lewin still has time to establish himself as a serious alternative, a high-quality back-up. When he came on as a substitute against Uruguay in March, it was his first England appearance in almost five years.

Calvert-Lewin has 12 caps. In the five games he has started, he has scored four goals.

Article continues below

True, the field is thin, but when it comes to the fight to be considered as the main alternative to Kane, Calvert-Lewin should be winning it. And he has not got the confidence to shine on the grandest stages.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel asks to QUIT Man Utd immediately as club left completely stunned
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel asks to QUIT Man Utd immediately as club left completely stunned

Manchester United have received devastating news over the future of teenage prodigy JJ Gabriel after he asked to quit the club immediately

Michael Carrick concerned by Manchester derby goal decision

Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel had informed the club that he wants to cancel his registration with them immediately. The 15-year-old prodigy has sent a formal notice of his desire to become a free agent.

‌



The club do not believe the situation is irretrievable and has not yet accepted Gabriel's request. The youngster has played for the club since the age of 11, and United can challenge or reject Gabriel's request to cancel his registration.

‌



Last week, Gabriel wiped all of the images from his Instagram, leading to some concern. The youngster already lays claim to more than 800,000 followers on the social media website.

‌



Gabriel is not able to sign a professional contract until he turns 17, and scholarship agreements are not permitted until players turn 16. He is not currently in line to join another club immediately, despite Manchester City previously trying to tempt him away from Old Trafford.

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel wants to leave Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Premier League rules require all parties to come to an agreement to end a registration period early. “During your child’s registration period, their registration may only be cancelled if everyone agrees (the club, player and their parent/carer)," they state.

“If the parties don’t agree, then any person involved can also ask the Premier League to provide a binding decision on a termination request," the rules add.

Gabriel was part of United's pre-season preparations across the summer and featured against Atletico Madrid. United are said to have planned for the teenager to be part of the squad for Wednesday night’s Carabao Cup tie against Brighton.

‌



The attacker has scored five goals and provided two assists in just three games across Premier League 2 and the UEFA Youth League. At 15, he is already playing amongst his elders on a regular basis.

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel continues to impress at Manchester United and is on the fringes of the first team. (Image: (Photo by Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



United boss Michael Carrick has been impressed by Gabriel's abilities and has frequently attended youth matches to monitor the youngster and other talents. Speaking last month after watching Gabriel, the Carrick said: "I really enjoyed the game. You could see the quality.

"JJ is one of the boys. He's obviously got a really big talent. He's trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time. He's physically adapting to each step that he makes, and we're just continuing his development."

Last term, Gabriel became the youngest winner of United’s Jimmy Murphy young-player-of-the-year award, racking up 23 goals in as many appearances in the under-18 Premier League.

‌



Speaking after Gabriel's immense performance against Sabah this season, under-21s boss Adam Lawrence offered a ringing endorsement of the player's abilities. "Well, I think the first thing in my job is not to ruin him," he said.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has previously heaped praise on the teenager (Image: Alfie Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"So when you have a talented player like JJ and the other lads of course, you obviously don't want to stifle their freedom and their creativity. And I think essentially what you try and do is to set the team up to allow the talent to function and to play free at the right moments.

Article continues below

"Of course, it can't always be free and off the cuff in terms of some of the off-the-ball responsibilities that he's working on and some of the pressing things that he's thinking about.

"But again, in terms of how he plays properly and how he connects with other teammates at the top end of the pitch, he's just in a real good space. If you look at that game today, I think he's playing properly."

Sports.title: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola demands 'higher levels' as weekend performance called out
Sports.content:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola demands 'higher levels' as weekend performance called out

Liverpool underwhelmed at the weekend as they were held to a goalless draw by Fulham with Andoni Iraola demanding considerably more come Tuesday night against Tottenham

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola was not overly impressed with Liverpool's display at the weekend

Andoni Iraola admits Liverpool should be "aiming for higher performance levels" after their lacklustre draw with Fulham at the weekend.

‌



The Reds were held to a goalless draw by the Cottagers at Anfield, Fulham's first point of the season, as they struggled to find a way through the west Londoners.

‌



It means that Liverpool are already six points off the pace set by Arsenal and Manchester City and without a win across their two Premier League games at Anfield this season. Iraola is still very much trying to get his ideas across with his tenure still in its infancy.

‌



Their Carabao Cup clash with Tottenham presents the chance for improvement, but is also their fourth game in 11 games. Iraola refused to see that as any type of excuse, insisting that will happen regularly given the amount of competitions their in, and wants to see forward strides made on Saturday's stalemate.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said in his programme notes: "There is no point making excuses or complaining about the time that we have to recover. This kind of situation is going to happen many times this season, so we have to face it and make the best of it.

"This doesn't necessarily mean I expect us to be at our very best in every single game that we play, but we should certainly be aiming for higher performance levels than we were able to reach at the weekend and we should also be finding ways to win.

"I say this because we want to be playing in the Champions League for as long as we can this season and we also want to be in the cup competitions for as long as we can."

‌



View 2 Images The Reds couldn't find a way past Fulham at Anfield

The former Bournemouth has also hinted as changes, such is the relentlessness of the fixture list. "We have a number of players who deserve more minutes than I have been able to give them up to this point so that will come into my thinking, particularly as we also have players who have already given a lot," he said.

Liverpool's win in Europe over Atletico Madrid last week was their best result of the season so far, coming back from a goal down to beat the Spanish side. Iraola talked up the impact Anfield can have when they host Tottenham on Tuesday night.

Article continues below

The north Londoners have underwhelmed this season, failing to score in their four league outings. Their only success came in the Carabao Cup, where they beat Charlton.

Sports.title: Webb: VAR had 'tunnel vision' on Haaland which led to Enzo error
Sports.content:
Pro Ref chief Howard Webb says VAR missed Enzo Fernandez being offside for Erling Haaland's winning goal in the Manchester derby due to "tunnel vision".

Webb says he is "really disappointed" by the decision to award the goal, which was initially ruled out on the field due to Haaland being flagged offside.

VAR then checked the incident and determined the striker was onside but failed to account for Enzo Fernandez impacting play from an offside position.

Fernandez dived for the ball before it was steered home by Haaland, and despite severely hindering Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens, Fernandez's offside position was overlooked once the VAR officials had confirmed he had not touched the ball - even though a player can be offside without touching the ball.

Webb told Mic'd Up: "The on-field decision was not against Fernandez; it was against Haaland. When the VAR starts their check, they see that Haaland is actually onside by three centimetres.

"The VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he is onside but when he runs it through the full APP (attacking possession phase), he doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez.

"In that moment, he gets tunnel vision but it is down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel but unfortunately, that did not happen on this occasion.

"This goal should have been disallowed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was VAR confusion as Erling Haaland fired Man City ahead!

Match officials in Manchester derby Referee: Michael Oliver

VAR: Matt Donohue

Assistant VAR: Blake Antrobus

Fourth official: Paul Tierney

Assistant referees: Stuart Burt and Tim Wood

What the officials said...

Assistant VAR: Enzo, Enzo.

VAR: Possible offside.

Assistant VAR: I'm going to go offside, Haaland.

Referee: On-field decision is offside.

VAR: Checking the on-field decision of offside against Haaland. He's tight. He's onside, so now we need to check the full attacking possession phase (APP).

Haaland's in an onside position, but I need to check the full APP. Go back to see if [Iliman] Ndiaye is onside when it is flicked. Yes. Go, go, go, so it should be a goal.

No touch there [from Enzo Fernandez], confirm no touch. Clear gap. It's not a touch there is it? Goal.

Michael, confirming that you need to change your decision to goal. Haaland is in an onside position. Final decision is goal; check complete.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville slams VAR's decision to give Erling Haaland's goal in the Manchester derby

Webb: VAR had 'tunnel vision' on Haaland and missed Enzo offside

Pro Ref chief operating officer Howard Webb:

"We felt it was important that we acknowledged an error in the situation. We know that Erling Haaland was penalised for offside and wasn't in an offside position.

"We also know that Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, almost certainly interfered with the Manchester United defence and probably the goalkeeper.

"I was really disappointed with this outcome; we all were. None more than the officials. They take personal pride in what they do and they are hurting now after falling short in this situation. They will not be officiating until after the international break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick, Lisandro Martinez and Erling Haaland react to Manchester City's controversial winner against Manchester United

"We have reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen and they do not happen often. We want to ensure we are transparent and open.

"We have played the audio and footage to the club to let them know what happened. We will review the situation to understand what elements of the process fell down in this situation which meant we didn't get to the right outcome.

"Fernandez doesn't actually touch the ball, so he has not committed what we would call a factual offside offence of interfering with play.

Image: Offside law graphic shown during coverage of Manchester United's match against Man City

"But you can still be penalised even if you do not touch the ball. In this situation, as the ball comes across, we see Fernandez dive towards the ball and he gets close to it.

"That impacts [Lisandro] Martinez; he cannot come and clear the ball. It probably impacts [Senne] Lammens as well, he cannot dive in the way he would or sets himself for potential contact from Fernandez.

"It is impacting the defence in a couple of ways as a result of the actions he makes in the offside position."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher and former Coventry striker Jay Bothroyd dissect the biggest talking point of the weekend and ask how VAR got Erling Haaland's winner for Manchester City against rivals United so wrong

Analysis: If VAR can't get the easy ones right, why are we using it at all?

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:

Pro Ref should not get a pardon for simply admitting their mistake on this one. A full-scale review into how is what they owe the players and clubs involved given it determined the outcome of the game.

"VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Enzo Fernandez didn't play the ball," is what the Premier League's match centre posted on X in real time. The offside rule appears to have been forgotten here, or at least the full extent of it.

VAR do confirm "no touch" by Fernandez, but fail to recognise he is live in the move. That element is not subjective. The Man City midfielder clearly impacts both Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens and yet neither are mentioned.

Nor does Michael Oliver question it. Does he communicate with the linesman to determine who was actually flagged offside? Was it Fernandez, Haaland or both?

A chronological check of the incident with the correct laws applied would have simply finished with Fernandez. Instead, the video officials spent nearly three minutes presiding over a goal that most casual observers could determine should not have stood with just one replay.

There are no excuses for such a catastrophic failing, but it's probably worth labouring the point that, if forensic technology cannot stamp out even the most basic of officiating mistakes, should we be using it at all?

'No one is hurting more than VAR officials - they're human'

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"I do have an element of sympathy for the VAR and his assistant - they made a mistake. A lot of football fans, particularly Man Utd supporters, will feel it is an unforgivable mistake.

"If you are a VAR and officiating a game as big as the Manchester derby, you really should not be making mistakes of this magnitude.

"But having said that, human beings are human beings. No one is hurting more than the VAR and his assistant. I imagine they've had sleepless nights over this and are replaying what happened over and over again for weeks and months to come.

"Human beings make mistakes and on this occasion, two human beings made a really big mistake which I'm sure they're going to regret for a long time."

Sports.title: Webb: Foden red justified but Fernandes escaped yellow for 'petulant' kick
Sports.content:
Pro Ref chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send off Phil Foden in the Manchester derby but revealed VAR could not intervene to caution Bruno Fernandes for the "petulant" kick that sparked the altercation.

Foden was sent off for violent conduct in Man City's 1-0 win at Old Trafford after kicking out at Fernandes after he was fouled by the Man Utd captain.

Fernandes escaped punishment after seemingly initiating the incident with a kick on Foden before the City forward reacted.

However, there appeared to be confusion during the VAR review of the incident as the officiating team checked for a possible Man Utd penalty after Enzo Fernandez's challenge on Youri Tielemans.

While referee Michael Oliver was brandishing the red card for Foden, VAR official Matt Donohue can be heard discussing the penalty while also saying: "Who has been sent off and for what?" shortly after.

Donohue is then alerted by his assistants to analyse Fernandes' kick on Foden, which initiated the melee between the two players.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Phil Foden was sent off after a clash with Bruno Fernandes!

The confusing VAR process surrounding Foden's red card

Referee: No, no. The ball, in my opinion, is played by Enzo Fernandez. Feet are side by side.

VAR: Checking possible penalty. One more angle to prove he's definitely played the ball. It looks like he's played the ball.

Phil Foden then kicks out at Bruno Fernandes after being caught by the Man Utd captain and is sent off shortly after.

Match officials in Manchester derby Referee: Michael Oliver

VAR: Matt Donohue

Assistant VAR: Blake Antrobus

Fourth official: Paul Tierney

Assistant referees: Stuart Burt and Tim Wood

Assistant VAR: Possible kick-out as well.

Referee: Has he kicked him there?

VAR: Confirm here you think that Enzo has definitely played the ball and that this is no penalty.

Assistant VAR: Possible violent conduct.

VAR: Okay and then he's gone red card. So, I would say no penalty there, he definitely plays the ball, yeah? Okay and now we need to look at the rest, okay?

So, who has been sent off here and for what?

Assistant VAR: It was for a kick-out. It looks like he's given a foul and then the legs came up.

VAR: Michael [referee], the penalty is checked and cleared. Just confirm your on-field decision in terms of discipline here, please.

Referee: Red card, Phil Foden. Kick out into the body of Bruno [Fernandes]. The foul is by Bruno on Phil. I think he's in a tangle and when they are separating, I think Phil kicks him. But they will check.

VAR: That looks like a clear red card to me. Secondary movement, watch broadcast. Okay, happy to confirm?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dermot Gallagher and Jay Bothroyd discuss whether Bruno Fernandes and Phil Foden should have both been sent off

Red card. Happy to confirm? Confirming the red card for Manchester City 47. A kick to the midriff with two feet.

Just roll through to check that Bruno does nothing. I'm absolutely certain he doesn't. No, he kicks the ball; it's fine.

Assistant VAR: No, the other one [Bruno's first kick]. That's not what they're talking about. That is the one they're talking about.

VAR: Minimal, minimal. That's not for us; that's fine.

Assistant VAR: Yeah, I agree.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane and Micah Richards debate the Phil Foden red card

Webb: Foden decision was correct but Fernandes avoids 'petulant' yellow

Pro Ref chief operating officer Howard Webb:

"I agree with the red card for Phil Foden for violent conduct. He kicks out with force into the upper body of Bruno Fernandes. We saw a player sent off for Aston Villa, Joao Gomes, for a similar thing.

"That is seen by the referee on the field and that is the on-field decision.

"When you look at the footage, there is the petulant kick from Fernandes into the back side of Foden. It is more petulant than violent. To be violent conduct, it has to have excessive force or brutality.

"When you look at that at full speed, it does not have that element. It would be a yellow card and VAR cannot step in to give a yellow.

"If all of it was missed and nothing was given against Foden, then VAR could step in and see Foden's actions for a possible red card and capture Fernandes' yellow card action. Because the referee gave the red card, that option is not open for VAR."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher has his say on the controversial decisions from Sunday's Manchester derby...

Analysis: Fernandes deserved equal treatment to Foden

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:

The review of this incident is all over the place. But the most alarming element is the reading of Bruno Fernandes's part.

Lead VAR official Matt Donohue is distracted by a previous incident in real time.

His VAR assistant leads with "possible kick out" by Foden. The immediacy of the on-field decision from Michael Oliver to send Foden off is the determining factor here. Oliver acts fast which suggests he is sure, and so VAR allows the call to stand.

The bar for intervention by VAR has been deliberately lifted higher for subjective decisions, remember, to avoid re-refereeing of games. This remains a grey area but less VAR interference is a good thing in my book.

Most can accept that Oliver's decision to dismiss Foden is not a "clear and obvious error" given where he makes contact with Fernandes. Whether it meets the threshold for "violent conduct" is of course open to interpretation.

What the VAR room failed to spot, however, is the trigger for Foden's reaction. Why is that not scrutinised in more detail?

"I'm absolutely certain he doesn't [do anything]," Donohue says of Fernandes's involvement. In reality, the Man Utd captain is the first offender and Foden's kick was retaliation for the kick he received after being fouled.

The decision not to punish Fernandes for the exact same action Foden is red-carded for is surely a huge oversight. Both deserved equal treatment in my opinion, especially important as Oliver clearly missed the first part from his position on the pitch. There is never any mention of it.

VAR's job is to alert him. Isn't that what the pitchside monitor is there for?

Sports.title: Bentley: Benn can 'skip the queue' for middleweight world title shot
Sports.content:
Conor Benn could get another world title shot if he returns to action at middleweight.

Denzel Bentley, the WBO world champion at 160lbs, is open to fighting Benn.

Benn twice boxed his family rival, Chris Eubank Jr, at middleweight before boiling back down to welterweight to challenge Ryan Garcia for the WBC title.

Garcia hammered Benn inside two rounds, with Benn now expected to return to middleweight.

Bentley, elevated to full world champion after claiming the WBO interim title with a storming performance against Endry Saavedra in April, would relish the prospect of defending his belt against Benn.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Toe2Toe, Barry Jones reflects on Conor Benn's defeat to Ryan Garcia

"Although the public might not think he deserves another world title shot in my eyes I feel like his profile is big enough for him to skip the queue," Bentley told Sky Sports.

"It's unfair but that's the sport we're in. Obviously it's beneficial for me, especially financially, so 100 per cent that's the fight I would take. I've never had any beef with Conor, we've always been cool.

"But if he is coming to the 160lb division, he goes from a companion to a potential challenger," he added.

Image: Denzel Bentley is now the WBO middleweight world champiomn. (Erik Verduzco/Las Vegas Review-Journal via AP)

"Firstly he needs to get himself right, well and fit. I think he should take a lot of time off and recover. I don't think there's any rush for him to get back into a boxing ring or even a gym. That weight cut was a fight in itself for him I think. Probably took a lot out of himself.

"Once he's well and fit, if he decides to move up to 160lbs and he does want the challenge, I think that's probably a conversation we can probably have ourselves: 'If you want to do this, let's push for it.'"

Bentley though had a warning for him. "I think I'm dangerous for anyone. I'm a lot bigger than him and I can punch."

But he added: "I think he will be a lot better with the extra weight.

"I think at 160lbs he'll be a lot more fuelled. But, listen, I punch as well and there were a lot of flaws in his game that night that I could exploit."
