Sports.title: Liverpool v Tottenham Hotspur: Carabao Cup third round – live
Sports.content:
now 16.18 EDT 57 min: Spurs make a double change, replacing Udogie and Bentancur with Fernandes and … Andy Robertson, who gets one hell of an ovation on his return to Anfield. Robertson keeps his gameface on, and he’ll be determined to do a job for his new club, but inside he’ll be having some feelings. Share

2m ago 16.16 EDT 56 min: Mac Allister has a chance to shoot from the edge of the D, but turns it down. It was on. Share

3m ago 16.15 EDT 55 min: Spurs respond well, pushing Liverpool back up the pitch, Tosin unleashing a low drive that fizzes wide of the left-hand post. Mamardashvili had it covered. Share

3m ago 16.14 EDT GOAL! Liverpool 2-0 Tottenham Hotspur (Gakpo 54) Ngumoha cuts in from the right and rolls across to Kerkez, who cushions the ball back to Mac Allister. No shot this time. Mac Allister finds Gakpo inside the box on the left. Gakpo takes a touch inside and lashes a shot across Dubravka and into the right-hand side of the net. No stopping that! Share

5m ago 16.13 EDT 53 min: Spurs get their foot on the ball for the first time in the second half. Sterile domination. But when they finally turn it over … Share

7m ago 16.11 EDT 51 min: Gakpo accidentally stands on Bentancur’s instep as the two battle for a loose ball. That’s a sore one, and it takes a moment for the Spurs midfielder to recover. But he’s up again soon enough. Share

9m ago 16.08 EDT 49 min: Koumas and McConnell have done a good job of leading the Liverpool press so far this evening. Spurs don’t look comfortable passing out from the back. Andoni Iraola will be hoping Alexander Isak is on the bench taking reams of notes. Share

11m ago 16.06 EDT 47 min: Given Gomez’s unfortunate injury record, hopefully his withdrawal is merely a matter of managing minutes. Those were his first 45 of the season. And he did take a whack on the head midway through, which won’t have helped. Share

13m ago 16.05 EDT Liverpool get the second half started. They’ve made one change, Jacquet coming on for Gomez. A reminder that if the game ends level after 90 minutes, there will be no extra time. It’ll be straight to penalties. Share

19m ago 15.59 EDT Half-time postbag. “At least you can’t accuse Roberto De Zerbi of parking the bus. No. It’s no use throwing players under a parked bus” – Justin Kavanagh “What a week for Liverpool! Ian ‘Mac the Mouth’ McCulloch and Echo & The Bunnymen are releasing a new album, and Alexis ‘Mac the Foot’ Mac Allister is scoring goals for fun at Anfield” – Peter Oh “Re: Andy (not that one) Flintoff, I recently saw correspondence from Andy Flintoff to the paper and thought, I bet it’s not that one. Is tonight’s Andy Flintoff not that one, or not that one or that one?” – Craig Fawcett Share

23m ago 15.54 EDT The doctor will see you now. “Thanks for your comment about colourblind supporters on 20 minutes,” begins Euan Lawson. “The Premier League have largely sorted appalling kit clashes out, and so I wonder if it’s a Carabao Cup thing. Yes, I can confirm, as a colourblind person, that the game is almost unwatchable. Or more unwatchable than normal with any game featuring Spurs. Red-green colourblindness affects one in 12 blokes - pretty much one in every men’s football team. It’s a nonsense that Spurs aren’t in white here. “Also a message for Adam Kent Ibáñez - it might be worth double-checking that he’s not colourblind. A lot of men get through life without realising and it can have health consequences: spotting blood in various bodily emissions can be missed and we all know those kind of things needs checking. Awareness can help. (I’m a GP.)” Share

27m ago 15.50 EDT HALF TIME: Liverpool 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur Mac Allister blazes the free kick over the bar, and that’s the end of an open and entertaining first half. The Argentinian scored a fine goal, both keepers have made one crucial stop, and Kudus has missed a sitter. It’s been fun. Share

29m ago 15.49 EDT 45 min +3: … but now Bentancur is booked for nudging the in-flight Gakpo from behind, just to the right of the D. With Szoboszlai on the bench, Mac Allister looks in the mood to pull rank here. He prepares to take. Share

30m ago 15.48 EDT 45 min +2: Senesi barges aggressively into McConnell, having arrived late for a 50-50. The referee, having just booked Frimpong and Marmoush for bugger all, decides a lecture is enough punishment this time. Share

32m ago 15.45 EDT 45 min: There will be two additional minutes tacked onto the end of this first half. Share

34m ago 15.44 EDT 43 min: Gomez goes long. Senesi heads back to Dubravka, who claims on the edge of his box, but only just in time, with Gakpo lurking. That was a risky ball back. Share

35m ago 15.43 EDT 41 min: Now Marmoush goes into the book for clipping McConnell a little bit late. That was a free kick, nothing more. Marmoush as deflated as Frimpong. The referee getting a bit card-happy here. Share

37m ago 15.41 EDT 40 min: Frimpong wins a battle with Tel down the Tottenham left … and is booked for nothing at all. Aurajo’s yellow card was as obvious as it gets; this one not so much, and Frimpong is understandably non-plussed. Share

37m ago 15.40 EDT 39 min: McConnell and Koumas combine down the inside-right channel, the latter cutting back for Mac Allister, six yards out. Mac Allister can’t sort his feet, the ball clanking off his shin and wide right. Share

39m ago 15.39 EDT 38 min: A Liverpool corner on the left leads to a second on the right. From that one, hit long, Koumas crosses low from the left. Had Gakpo taken a better touch, he’d have been spinning and shooting from eight yards. But there’s no better touch. Share

40m ago 15.38 EDT 36 min: Araujo is booked for the clearest of pull-backs on Marmoush. Seconds before, McConnell had been clumsily bundled over in the box from behind by Senesi. No penalty. VAR might have taken a look at that, you know. But there’s no VAR. Share

42m ago 15.35 EDT 34 min: Koumas nearly gets in ahead of Tosin down the left. Tosin turns the ball behind for a corner. A smart routine between Mac Allister and Kerkez leads to the former whipping into the middle. Ngumoha can’t win a header, then when the ball breaks to Nyoni, the young midfielder’s shot is blocked. There are definitely more goals in this. Share

44m ago 15.34 EDT 33 min: The loudest cheer of the night so far – apart from the goal, though there’s not much in it – as Andy Robertson warms up and is serenaded by his old fans. Share

45m ago 15.33 EDT 32 min: Bergvall and Udogie combine neatly down the left, Liverpool’s defence all over the shop. Udogie whips a low cross into the middle. Kudus gets in ahead of Kerkez, six yards out, and has to score … but somehow blazes over the bar. What a miss! Share

46m ago 15.31 EDT 30 min: Marmoush curls the corner to the near stick. Koumas bashes it clear with an authoritative header. Meanwhile here’s Andy (Not That One) Flintoff: “After a summer of unwanted US innovations into football (effectively splitting the game into quarters, the ultra-long half-time show for the final), one which we could import into football that would be welcomed is NFL’s colour system, where one team plays in dark shirts and one in light for maximum contrast.” Share

48m ago 15.30 EDT 29 min: Marmoush wins another free kick, getting properly clattered this time, by Mac Allister out on the right touchline. He curls it into the mixer, forcing Gomez to eyebrow out for a corner on the left. He takes a whack from Tosin, foreheads clashing, but he’ll be fine to continue. Share

50m ago 15.28 EDT 27 min: Marmoush picks off a loose pass from Gomez, and guards it from McConnell, who can’t stop clanking into the Spurs striker’s back, 25 yards out. He goes over easily for a cheap free kick, then curls the set piece he’d won harmlessly wide left of the target. View image in fullscreen Tottenham Hotspur's Omar Marmoush fires his free kick wide of the Liverpool goal. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.50 EDT

51m ago 15.26 EDT 25 min: That’ll have settled Liverpool, and suddenly Spurs are subdued. To be fair to Liverpool, they’d been growing into the game before opening the scoring. Share

52m ago 15.25 EDT 23 min: A fortunate deflection for Liverpool there, and they’d been second best for the most part, but what a finish by Mac Allister, who did something fairly similar when Arne Slot’s side sealed the 2024-25 Premier League title here against these opponents. Pinged towards the top right, Dubravka rooted and with no chance. Share

55m ago 15.23 EDT GOAL! Liverpool 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur (Mac Allister 21) Gakpo cuts in from the left and finds Ngumoha on the other flank. Ngumoha dribbles infield and his low pass into the box is deflected towards Mac Allister, who meets it on the edge of the box by opening his body and power-steering a sidefooter into the top right. Delicious finish! View image in fullscreen All eyes are on the ball as a shot by Liverpool’s Alexis Mac Allister heads towards the Spurs goal. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters View image in fullscreen Liverpool fans and Mac Allister celebrate. Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.35 EDT

1h ago 15.21 EDT 20 min: Ngumoha tries another dribble down the right but the road is blocked this time. “Am I just getting old or are these kits too similar to tell apart?” wonders Adam Kent Ibáñez. It’s certainly not very thoughtful to colour-blind supporters. A red-white contrast would work just fine; red-navy not so much. Share

1h ago 15.18 EDT 18 min: Kerkez bustles down the left and makes something out of nothing, bursting into a bit of space before digging out a cross that’s too high for McConnell in the middle. The crowd enjoyed that, though, and perhaps Liverpool are beginning to find a foothold in this match. Share

1h ago 15.17 EDT 16 min: Ngumoha drops a shoulder to make himself a pocket of space 30 yards out. He slips a pass down the inside-right channel for Koumas, who spins Senesi but can’t force his shot past Dubravka, who spreads himself to block. Both keepers have now made a fine goal-saving stop. Share

1h ago 15.15 EDT 14 min: Sky flash up a stat: Spurs have made 20 successful passes in the opposition’s final third to Liverpool’s three. Slightly surprised Liverpool have made that many, to be honest. They’ve been taken aback by Tottenham’s positive start. Share

1h ago 15.13 EDT 13 min: A rare sortie for Liverpool in Spurs territory, as Ngumoha probes down the right and crosses. The ball’s deflected into the arms of Dubravka, who has otherwise had nothing to do. Share

1h ago 15.12 EDT 11 min: Udogie burns down the left and fires a low cross into the Liverpool box. Bergvall is free, eight yards out. He opens his body and sidefoots powerfully towards the bottom left. Mamardashvili, diving the other way, sticks up a leg and blocks. That’s a spectacular reaction stop, and has cost Bergvall a certain goal. Share

1h ago 15.11 EDT 10 min: Spurs are dominating these early exchanges. They’re winning everything in the middle of the park. A third of the play so far has been in Liverpool’s final third. Kudus cuts in from the right and shoots; Gomez blocks. Then shanks a clearance out for a throw, much to the Kop’s chagrin. Liverpool looking as nervous as Spurs are assured. View image in fullscreen Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall surges forwards at Liverpool. Photograph: Jon Super/AP Share Updated at 15.44 EDT

1h ago 15.08 EDT 8 min: It’s suddenly raining reasonably heavily on Merseyside. Perfect conditions for some slick passing. So having said that, Gray throws long down the right touchline, forcing Gomez to poke behind for the first corner of the match. Frimpong and Nyoni combine to clear Kudus’s far-post delivery. Share

1h ago 15.06 EDT 6 min: A bit of space for Koumas down the right. He’s got no real options in the box, but wouldn’t have found them anyway, as he loops a harmless ball over to the opposite flank and away from danger. Share

1h ago 15.06 EDT 5 min: Gakpo drives with purpose down the inside-left channel, but is stopped in his tracks by a fine sliding block from Bergvall. Spurs have started confidently at both ends of the park. Share

1h ago 15.05 EDT 4 min: Kerkez was outside the box, but that’s a reminder of there being no VAR tonight. No interminable check to make sure. Share

1h ago 15.04 EDT 3 min: Gallagher scampers down the right and crosses. Kerkez slides along the ground, his arm well above his head, and deflects the ball to Mamardashvili … off his hand. A free kick just outside the box. Kudus crosses, but Araujo deals with it. He tries again and the keeper claims this time. Share

1h ago 15.02 EDT 1 min: There have been a few concerns about Mamardashvili’s distribution with his feet … and he whistles his first pass, a simple one towards Kerkez on the left, out of play. He looks suitably sheepish. No real harm done, though. Share

1h ago 15.00 EDT After a quick blast of You’ll Never Walk Alone, Tottenham Hotspur get the ball rolling. They’re kicking towards the Kop in this first half. Meanwhile Ian Copestake replies to krishnamoorthy v: “I could have crossed the road faster but I have to get my kicks somehow.” Share

1h ago 14.59 EDT The teams are out at Anfield. Liverpool the red men, Spurs the lilywhites, exactly as it should be Spurs in dark navy with diagonal swirls of electric pink, bright orange, and neon purple. A fine atmosphere at Anfield; Andy Robertson seemed super-pleased to catch up with a few of his old pals. That was a sweet moment. Not long now for the rerun of the 1982 final! When Liverpool won the League Cup four years in a row Read more Share

1h ago 14.50 EDT Pre-match postbag. “Great to see Joe Gomez back. However, I predict a muscle strain on 23 minutes sadly” – Jesse Davies “It (probably) won’t happen but would anything be funnier than 0-0 after 90 minutes, then Tottenham missing their first three pens and Liverpool going through?” – Dave Estherby “I have seen a lot many optimists in my life but none so optimistic as you who equates fun with Spurs. Watching Tottenham play these days is equivalent to watching an arthritic old man cross the road at a signal when you are already running late” – krishnamoorthy v Share

2h ago 14.44 EDT Andoni Iraola speaks to Sky Sports. “We decided to change a lot of the team … we needed fresh legs … we have a lot of players willing to have a good performance … get us to the next round … also looking forward to seeing those players … I am sure they will take that chance … it’s a great chance to see [the younger players] … if we put them in, it’s because we think they are ready to help us and ready to perform … we will get a lot of information from this game … it is a matter of execution and keeping calm … I trust them … I hope they do well … we know we will face a strong team … but I trust my players.” Share

2h ago 14.41 EDT This is all a bit of a back-of-envelope scribble, so if I’ve forgotten someone you’ll have to sue me*, but it’s just occurred to me that quite a lot of the players on the team-sheets tonight have already tasted League Cup glory. For Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo, Joe Gomez, Ryan Gravenberch, Waturo Endo, Kostas Tsimikas and James McConnell played in either the 2022 or 2024 final victories over Chelsea, with Alisson, Trey Nyoni and Lewis Koumas getting medals for being on the bench in 2024, also Dominik Szoboszlai despite being injured. In addition, Alexander Isak scored for Newcastle in their win over Liverpool in 2025. As for Spurs, Andy Robertson is the only one of tonight’s squad to have played and won a final (for Liverpool) while Omar Marmoush and Savio were on the bench earlier this year for Manchester City’s victory over Arsenal, just as Martin Dubravka watched on from the dugout while Newcastle won in 2025. Sandro Tonali isn’t involved tonight, but he did play in that Newcastle victory, and can tell everyone about it when they get back. * Please do not sue me. Share

2h ago 14.13 EDT Roberto De Zerbi speaks to Sky Sports. “I am lucky I have a great squad … many very good players … changing the first XI, I hope we don’t change the quality of the players, I am sure they are the same level … I would like to see the goals … the same attitude of the first 30 minutes against Everton … we have the qualities enough to score … it’s a tough moment … no pressure, but we play to win the games … playing at Anfield against Liverpool is always tough … but my focus is on my team … after one month of working together … keep our eyes on our goal … our organisation of the play and nothing else.” Share

2h ago 14.04 EDT Both teams make a slew of changes from their Premier League selections at the weekend. The only survivor from the XI that started Liverpool’s 0-0 draw with Fulham is Ronald Araujo. He’ll move from right back to form a central defensive pairing with Joe Gomez, who returns from his latest injury lay-off. Spurs retain three members of their starting XI for the goalless draw against Everton. Rodrigo Bentancur, Omar Marmoush and captain Archie Gray go again. A couple of LFC old boys are on the bench: Dominic Solanke and Andrew Robertson, the latter having made 378 appearances for the Reds. Expect emotion if Robertson gets minutes. Share

2h ago 13.49 EDT The teams Liverpool: Mamardashvili, Frimpong, Araujo, Gomez, Kerkez, Nyoni, Mac Allister, Ngumoha, McConnell, Gakpo, Koumas.

Subs: Alisson, Endo, Jacquet, Szoboszlai, Isak, Munoz, Barcola, Gravenberch, Chambers. Tottenham Hotspur: Dubravka, Gray, Tosin, Senesi, Udogie, Bentancur, Bergvall, Kudus, Gallagher, Tel, Marmoush.

Subs: Kinsky, Robertson, van Hecke, Maddison, Savio, Fernandes, Solanke, Davies, van de Ven. Referee: Andrew Madley (West Yorkshire) Share Updated at 14.10 EDT

Sports.title: Howard Webb says accidental handball law ‘a nonsense’ and calls for reform
Sports.content:
Howard Webb has described the law around accidental handball as “a bit of a nonsense” and called for its reform to stop referees being drawn into “ridiculous situations”.

The chief refereeing officer for English football made his remarks on Tuesday, when he also fronted up over the error that allowed Manchester City to win Sunday’s Manchester derby. Webb said he was “really disappointed” with the video assistant referee call that failed to spot Enzo Fernández interfering with play from an offside position before Erling Haaland scored the only goal.

Speaking on Match Officials Mic’d Up, Webb reviewed a number of controversial incidents from the Premier League season. He said the buildup to an Ipswich own goal at Manchester United, where the ball hit Harry Maguire’s hand before he took a shot that deflected off Jacob Greaves and into the net, highlighted problems with the handball law.

“It’s a bit of a nonsense, isn’t it?” Webb said. “If [Maguire] strikes the ball beautifully into the top corner, then the goal gets disallowed. [But] he skews his shot, it becomes an own goal, and it’s awarded.”

The handball law says it is an offence “if a player scores in the opponent’s goal directly from their hand/arm [or] immediately after the ball has touched their hand/arm, even if accidental”. If another player touches the ball before it goes in, however, only a deliberate handball would lead to play being brought back. Webb said he believed this was the wrong approach.

“The law should change away from that idea,” he said. “We’re in this ridiculous situation whereby the goal is allowed to stand because it’s an own goal. You also get officials having to work out: was the shot on target, was it not on target? The worst-case scenario for us is that the officials decide that the ball is going wide and it’s an own goal, but then later on the goal is attributed to the player that scored, whose arm it hit. So, I think we ought to look at this and just allow the officials to determine whether it’s a normal handball offence. Did he make himself bigger? Did he deliberately handle the ball? And I don’t think [Maguire] does those things in this situation.”

Webb, who has promised greater transparency from Pro Ref, is increasingly expected to give a public verdict on controversial decisions and it was not a surprise to find Match Officials Mic’d Up scheduled for TV 48 hours after the farrago in the Manchester derby.

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland celebrates after his goal in the derby was cleared to stand. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

The VAR Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus were stood down from their duties on Monday, after Pro Ref acknowledged “an error of judgment” in assessing City’s winning goal. Donohue was called on to check the decision to disallow Haaland’s 60th-minute strike for offside. Using semi-automated offside technology, Donohue was able to establish that the striker was onside and he overturned ­Oliver’s call. But he failed to spot Fernández had influenced play from an offside position, an ­infringement which Pro Ref said should have led him to recommend an on-field review.

Webb said it was “important” this error had been acknowledged. “I was really disappointed with this outcome, we all are, none more so than the officials themselves,” he said. “They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they’re obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They’ll not be officiating again until after the international break.”

Webb said that Donohue had got “tunnel vision” while assessing the lead-up to the goal, concentrating on Haaland and not Fernández, because the on-field decision was against Haaland. “Donohue doesn’t truly evaluate the full impact of Fernández’s position,” Webb said. “He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score. He doesn’t touch the ball, but he doesn’t truly evaluate other elements of offside. In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. He gets focused on Haaland, and it’s down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn’t happen.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Have laudable Leeds left the chaos behind them?
Sports.content:
THE DAMN FINE UNITED?

It’s been quite the stomach-churning white-knuckle ride for Leeds United over the past decade. Their fans have been forced to endure more highs, lows, loops, corkscrews and rolls than a thrill-seeking visitor on Nemesis Reborn at Alton Towers. There have been b@nter eras, multiple owners, near-misses, promotions, relegations and managerial churn. The Marcelo Bielsa years will always be remembered as fondly as the Thomas Christiansen months have been erased from collective memory. Under Jesse Marsch, Leeds secured dramatic final-day Premier League survival at Brentford, before dropping through the trapdoor the following season despite the best efforts of the High Performance American and Lower Performance Javi Gracia and Big Sam Allardyce.

Three years ago, they were taken over by 49ers Enterprises, a USA USA USA-based organisation pursuing the endearingly romantic notion of extending their “brand into sports, entertainment and technology, leveraging team capabilities in marketing and operations”. Ever since, Leeds have been on an upward trajectory and on Monday night they secured a statement 4-1 victory that suggested for the first time in over 10 years, a period of long overdue stability – if not total serenity, admittedly – may be about to reign over Elland Road for a couple of weeks at least.

Under what the media are now obliged to describe as the [insert pertinent day of the week here] night lights of Elland Road, Leeds didn’t so much beat Newcastle as give them a horse-whipping. Stronger, faster, hungrier and quicker to every ball, there was one sustained period of dominance after they’d already gone 2-0 up when they left their visitors quite literally chasing shadows around the floodlit pitch. Watching his team concede another two goals before nabbing a late consolation, Matthias Jaissle looked shellshocked by their poor performance in the face of such an onslaught. “We couldn’t match the intensity and you see how difficult it can be to win a game in the Premier League,” sighed the German, whose promising start as Eddie Howe’s successor could scarcely have come to a more abrupt halt.

Despite admitting he prefers to celebrate a win by enjoying a hot beverage and cake on his sofa, such was the dominance of Leeds over Newcastle that Daniel Farke might have been tempted to unleash the inner “fire beast” to which he has previously alluded and swing from the chandeliers. “It’s important we stay humble, down to earth and can’t allow ourselves to be too big-time or too carried away,” he parped, suggesting a quiet night in with a mug of tea and a couple of accompanying fat rascals lay in store. Having seen their team leapfrog fellow title contenders Hull City to go third in the table, one suspects the post-match celebrations of many fans will not have been as abstemious. A tough bunch to please and often with good reason, they are happily marching on together. Onwards, upwards and in the direction of Arsenal’s Emirates Stadium in just two matches’ time.

View image in fullscreen Daniel Farke delivering his trademark nice touch. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Scott Murray from 8pm for hot Milk Cup minute-by-minute coverage of Liverpool 1-0 Tottenham, while Taha Hashim will be at the wheel for all the latest updates from Ipswich 1-3 Arsenal.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“We cannot conduct a serious analysis when death threats are involved. Something suspicious is happening and it needs to be investigated. The sport has been tainted. My goalkeeper received threats against his life, his wife and his mother – he was told that if he didn’t pay a specific sum or concede three goals, they would be killed” – Guabirá head coach Leonardo Egüez claims that Juan Manuel Ferrel received death threats before their 6-0 defeat by Club Always Ready in the Bolivian top flight. “Football must not be tainted,” said Club Always Ready’s legal adviser Marcelo Ortiz. “We will ask the public prosecutor’s office to investigate so that the sport’s integrity is preserved.”

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling could face prison for reckless driving while using nitrous oxide
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and could be sent to prison after driving his ­Lamborghini for more than an hour on motorways during rush hour while inhaling nitrous oxide.

The former Chelsea and Manchester City forward stood in the dock to accept three charges before ­Basingstoke magistrates court heard how he embarked on a ­prolonged period of reckless driving on the M25 and M3, inhaling nitrous oxide ­balloons, before crashing his £270,000 car. Sterling was disqualified from driving and bailed until 25 November, when his sentence will either be determined or referred to the crown court.

Sterling also admitted possession of nitrous oxide and refusing to ­provide a specimen.

The maximum term for Sterling would be two years in prison, although a sentence of 12 to 18 months is considered more likely and, with mitigation, that could be suspended.

Simon Jones, prosecuting, told the court one witness had “genuine concerns the driver might kill someone” and described Sterling’s driving as “absolutely horrendous”.

“As she moved past the vehicle she thought the airbag had been deployed, it was a large white deflated balloon,” Jones said. “She had no idea if the driver could see ahead.”

View image in fullscreen Raheem Sterling (centre) arriving at Basingstoke magistrates court on Tuesday. Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PA

Between 7.45am and 8.52am on 28 May, police received multiple calls reporting dangerous driving – shortly after Sterling had returned to England after a loan at Feyenoord, where he had attempted to revive his career.

Dashcam footage provided to police by one witness showed Sterling’s car swerving between lanes and almost colliding with the central reservation. Witnesses reported seeing the driver inhaling balloons while driving.

After leaving the M3, the Lamborghini veered off the carriageway on the A327 near the Minley interchange in Hampshire. All four tyres blew out and there was damage to the bodywork. Body-worn footage from officers attending the scene, played in court, showed Sterling, 31, sitting in the passenger seat with two canisters on his lap before confirming he had been driving.

Jones said Sterling appeared keen to move a deflated balloon from beside him on to the back seat. His saliva was tested and no presence of cannabis or cocaine was found, but he later refused to provide a blood sample to test for other substances.

Quick Guide How do I 

Another witness told police they had seen the Lamborghini driving erratically at 1.10am. They reported it entering a drive-through at “alarming speed”, Jones said, and saw the driver holding an inflated balloon.

After his arrest, Sterling was taken to Basingstoke investigation centre. “During the process he had disclosed to staff that he had a problem with nitrous oxide,” Jones said.

Sterling failed a series of impairment tests, including walking in a straight line without swaying and placing his fingertip on the end of his nose. He was also asked to judge 30 seconds with his eyes closed but recorded 52.

Jones said Sterling “appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting” during the tests. “His eyelids were drooping, consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.”

The former England international, who won 82 caps between 2012 and 2022 and played in five major tournaments, was taken to a medical room where he refused to provide a blood sample without providing a reasonable excuse and despite repeated and clear warnings.

At 5.13pm, Sterling was interviewed with a legal representative present. A signed, prepared statement was read out in which he said he had not slept all night and was tired and confused. He then answered “no comment” to officers’ questions.

Jason Bartfield KC for the defence did not dispute this was a top-category case, given the prolonged driving and clear serious impairment. Bartfield cautioned, however, that there would have been “short periods” of “serious impairment”, compared with consuming cannabis or alcohol.

View image in fullscreen Raheem Sterling after being stopped by police in May. Photograph: Crown Prosecution Service/PA

Bartfield did not accept the car damage was serious, describing it as “relatively superficial” and “minor scratching” alongside the blown tyres. He also argued that the fact there were two canisters in Sterling’s lap when police arrived showed “this was very much not a case of trying to conceal anything from them”.

The court was not told the full mitigating circumstances, but ­Bartfield said: “Clearly there is extensive ­personal mitigation. Voluntary steps have been taken to address them. I hope this has weight with the court.”

District judge Kirsty Allman ordered a pre-sentence report and adjourned the hearing. She said she had not decided whether to retain jurisdiction or commit sentencing to the crown court. A magistrates court cannot impose a sentence of more than 12 months.

“I’m going to release you on unconditional bail,” she said. “If you don’t attend, a warrant will be issued for your arrest. I’m going to disqualify you from driving as of today. You must not drive a motor vehicle on the road as of today. I will determine the period if I sentence you, otherwise it will be for the crown court. You must not drive while disqualified – if you drive while disqualified you will be committing a prisonable offence.”

Sports.title: Manchester United shocked as talented youngster JJ Gabriel asks to leave
Sports.content:
Manchester United have been left confused and shocked by the news that the talented 15-year-old player JJ Gabriel has asked to leave the club, a day before he was to be included in the first-team squad to face Brighton.

Gabriel could have become United’s youngest player in the Carabao Cup third-round tie at Old Trafford on Wednesday. But the Guardian understands he has asked for his registration to be cancelled.

United are unsure what has prompted this decision and believe they have done everything they can to show Gabriel and his family there is a pathway to the first team. Those efforts have included meetings with Ruben Amorim, when the Portuguese was head coach, and Sir Alex Ferguson.

United believe the situation, first reported by the Telegraph, is rectifiable given the time remaining on Gabriel’s contract. Club officials say the player has a deal to the end of the season and cannot be deregistered despite his request. The north London-born Gabriel cannot sign a professional contract until he turns 17 in October next year, but can sign a scholarship agreement when he turns 16.

Gabriel, who has been with United since the age of 11, has emerged as one of the most exciting prospects at Carrington in years, scoring a hatful of goals for the youth teams, most recently a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut against Sabah last week. He regularly plays for older age groups at United, scoring 26 goals in 29 games last season, and has made two appearances for England Under-17s. Gabriel is also the most recent, and youngest, winner of United’s prestigious Jimmy Murphy young player of the year award. He has regularly trained with the first team.

Quick Guide Carrick say VAR blunder will fuel United Show Michael Carrick believes Manchester United will have an edge against Brighton in the Carabao Cup owing to the wrong video assistant referee decision that allowed Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s defeat by Manchester City. United host Fabian Hürzeler’s side on Wednesday aiming to bounce back after Haaland’s 60th-minute strike was judged to be legal by the VAR, who ruled that Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the buildup. Pro Ref admitted the goal should not have been allowed and that Matt Donohue, the VAR, had made the wrong decision. He has been stood down for this weekend's Premier League action. Carrick, speaking before Pro Ref’s statement, was asked whether his players would have an edge against Brighton owing to their annoyance at ruling. “It does give you something, when something like that happens, to use moving forward," the manager said. "The players have got an edge. They've shown that to me since I've been here. We've had setbacks, and they've bounced back particularly well and had some really good performances and good results." United have taken four points from their first four games. “We've got to move on [from City loss]; we've got to win games,” said Carrick. “We have done – we've won a lot of games, and we need to continue to do that. I understand it's a new season, and the points tally right now is not what we want it to be. I'm not hiding from that, but it's more of about getting back to winning games, that feeling, getting the habit. It's easier said than done, but we're capable of it.” Luke Shaw may be available after a knock. Jamie Jackson Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Speaking after that 5-0 win against Sabah, Adam Lawrence, United’s lead under-21 coach, said: “JJ is surrounded by people that really, really believe in him from the top of the club right the way through. He’s been at the club for so long. He’s got real good relationships with the players, with the staff, so I think over the course of time obviously that helps as well.

“At the moment, just in terms of his game, his games programme, his training programme, it’s about making sure that he’s getting the right exposure across different levels. We’re obviously not perfect but it’s definitely something we put a lot of thought into.”

Sports.title: Louisville’s Savannah DeMelo sues team doctors after cardiac arrest during game
Sports.content:
Racing Louisville midfielder Savannah DeMelo has filed a lawsuit against UofL Health and two named physicians for negligence after they allegedly failed to properly diagnose a heart condition before she suffered cardiac arrest in the first half of an NWSL game on 14 September 2025.

According to an screenshot of the complaint, the filing claims that UofL Health “failed to act as a reasonably prudent and competent medical practice … and such negligence was a substantial factor in causing [DeMelo] to suffer severe physical injuries, including, but not limited to, her cardiac arrest.”

When contacted by the Guardian, a clerk with the Jefferson Circuit Court confirmed that the case was filed on Tuesday morning – a year and a day after her on-field cardiac arrest.

Sources close to DeMelo and the club, speaking anonymously due to the sensitive nature of both her recovery and the filing, told the Guardian that Racing has already determined that it will not work with UofL Health after the current season. Neither named physician – including one listed on the club’s website as chief medical officer – is an employee of the club, instead working with the team as part of an agreement between the organizations. Racing is already in the process of finding a new medical partner ahead of the 2027 season.

The sources also disclosed that DeMelo, whose contract was set to expire at the end of this season, has reached a verbal agreement with Racing to keep her at the club. The deal is pending league approval and could be announced as soon as next week. DeMelo is nearing a return to competitive action, having resumed full training with her teammates this week. A source said the current timeline could have her involved as soon as 25 September’s match, in which Louisville will host the San Diego Wave.

A spokesperson for Racing Louisville declined to comment. UofL Health said it was unable to comment on pending litigation. A representative for DeMelo did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

DeMelo has spent her entire professional career with Louisville, selected fourth overall in the 2022 NWSL Draft. Her progressive approach in midfield and set-piece prowess made her a surprise pick for the United States’ roster at the 2023 Women’s World Cup, becoming the third player in USWNT history to make a World Cup squad without having previously been capped.

In late 2024, DeMelo was diagnosed with Graves’ disease, an autoimmune disorder which causes an overactive thyroid. The midfielder disclosed her diagnosis midway through the following season, having exited a game on 22 March 2025 citing dizziness and chest tightness. Six months later, DeMelo collapsed on the field during a game in Seattle. That made her the second NWSL player to have a heart scare during a game last season, with Angel City defender Savy King suffering a cardiac arrest on 9 May 2025.

Sports.title: From Segura to Maltby: six breakout stars from the Women’s Under-20 World Cup
Sports.content:
The 2026 Under-20 Women’s World Cup is entering the knockout stage in Poland and, after an intriguing group stage, we pick some of the young stars who have stood out.

Celia Segura (Spain and Barcelona)

Segura is no stranger to knockout football having helped Spain to silver at the Under-17 World Cup two years ago and finishing with the Bronze Ball and Bronze Boot. She has picked up the mantleagain as La Roja eased through their group. Her four goals against New Caledonia were an illustration of her pure scoring instinct and she has also played a key role with her high technical skills and instinctive ability to both make space for and find her teammates. Her back-heel assist to set up Pau Comendador against China was a memorable one. A product of the Barcelona academy, the 19-year-old forward made her debut for the senior side back in February and will return to Atlético Madrid for a season-long loan at the conclusion of this tournament.

Annika Paz (Argentina and Inter)

Paz has taken this tournament by storm with performances that have shown a maturity beyond her 17 years. She is one of a few stars in Poland who have already made their debut for their senior national team – she marked her first cap with a goal against Uruguay in 2025, becoming Argentina’s youngest ever goalscorer. Paz netted four goals against Benin here in Poland before also scoring the opener in Argentina’s dramatic 3-2 win over Mexico to send them through. Her pace, movement off the ball and finishing are exceptional, alongside her composure in front of goal. Having progressed from the River Plate pathway to the senior team, Paz made her move to Europe back in January to join Inter.

Rachel Maltby (England and Aston Villa)

After a breakthrough campaign with Aston Villa last season and now a second youth World Cup with England, it has been a memorable year for Maltby. With her four goals and an assist, the 19-year-old has played a crucial role here in England’s progress to the last 16. As she did at the under-17 edition of the tournament back in 2024, the 19-year-old has caught the eye with her assured, attacking performances down England’s left. Full of energy, composure and with an instinctive ability to time her runs into the box, she has displayed her versatility in switching between her more established full-back role and left wing with ease. Her three penalties, which she can take with either foot, are further examples of how mature she has become over the past 12 months.

Annabelle Chukwu (Canada and Notre Dame Fighting Irish)

There is plenty of excitement in Canada around this young forward. Chukwu changed the game from the bench with the opening goal in their 1-1 draw with England and then added two more in their 6-0 routing of Tanzania to send her side through to the knockout stage. Pacy and clinical, her direct transitional threat is second-to-none. Currently at university, the 19-year-old has excelled playing for the Notre Dame Fighting Irish and through the national youth pathways. Earning her name as a prolific goalscorer – she broke the record for most goals scored for Canada’s youth teams with 28 in 34 appearances – she received her first senior debut back in June and surely has her focus set on being part of Casey Stoney’s side at next summer’s World Cup in Brazil.

View image in fullscreen Annabelle Chukwu of Canada. Photograph: Mateusz Słodkowski/FIFA/Getty Images

Huang Jiaxin (China and Shanghai Shengli WFC)

The centre-back has been one of China’s clear standouts in Poland – not just for her efforts at the heart of the defence but also for her goalscoring ability. Her acceleration up the field and 12-minute hat-trick against New Caledonia illustrated not only her willingness to support her side further up the pitch but also her qualities as an instinctive finisher in front of goal. Her manager, Wang Jun, emphasised this versatility in an interview with Fifa. “She has own characteristics,” he said. “In the future, I hope that she can play in Europe and bring her skills to the senior national team.” At 20, that prospect is not far away, particularly with a World Cup for China on the horizon.

Evelin (Brazil and Santos)

Given Brazil’s performances so far in this tournament and with a home senior World Cup to come, it would have been a terrible decision not to include a Brazilian in this list. While there have been quite a few to choose from, 18-year-old Evelin has particularly impressed. She might be small in stature but there is nothing little about her game with her innate natural ability, energy and eye for a finish. She kicked off the tournament with two almost identical finishes against Tanzania and has also registered two assists to help her team cruise through to the last 16. Domestically, she came up through the ranks at Santos where she has progressed into the senior setup. She was part of the Brazil team that finished fourth at last year’s Under-17 World Cup and made her senior debut in April 2026.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi’s former Argentina teammate is now his head coach at Inter Miami after Javier Mascherano departure
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi’s former Argentina teammate is now his head coach at Inter Miami after Javier Mascherano departure

Lionel Messi can win another trophy at Inter Miami whilst playing for a different former teammate this week.

Inter Miami announced towards the end of August that they reached an agreement with Cristian 'Kily' Gonzalez regarding their vacancy.

2 Gonzalez has taken the reins at Inter Miami after Mascherano's exit Credit: Getty

Gonzalez has now officially arrived in Florida and begun his duties at the MLS club.

He has become the permanent successor to Javier Mascherano, who surprisingly resigned as head coach for personal reasons in April.

Mascherano made 414 appearances alongside Messi for the Argentina national team, their Olympic side and Barcelona.

They then won the MLS Eastern Conference and MLS Cup when the former was boss, with a new but fellow familiar face now in charge.

Gonzalez is in his fourth managerial role at Inter Miami after spells at Rosario Central, Union de Santa Fe and Club Atletico Platense.

Formerly a winger at clubs including Boca Juniors, Valencia and Inter Milan, he scored ten goals across 56 appearances for Argentina.

Two of his caps were won with Messi, with both coming during their qualification campaign for the 2006 World Cup.

Gonzalez is now set to work with the football icon yet again, this time in a different capacity as his head coach at Inter Miami.

His touchline debut comes on Wednesday night as they face Mexican side Cruz Azul in the 2026 Campeones Cup final.

The annual exhibition match is contested by the MLS champions and Mexican super cup (Campeon de Campeones) winners.

2 Messi could land his fourth honour in Inter Miami colours on Wednesday Credit: Getty

What trophies has Messi won at Inter Miami?

Just weeks after completing his shock move to North America in July 2023, Messi helped guide his new club to their first ever trophy.

He scored in the 1-1 Leagues Cup final draw with Nashville SC before Inter Miami triumphed with a dramatic 10-9 penalty shootout win.

Supporters' Shield glory followed in 2024 as the Floridian side had the best regular season in MLS with a league-record 74 points.

Inter Miami then lifted the MLS Cup in December with a 3-1 win over Vancouver Whitecaps, with Messi bagging two assists.

They will therefore win a fourth different honour if they beat Cruz Azul on Wednesday.

Another MLS Cup victory could follow later in the year as they are on course to qualify for round one of the play-offs by sitting second in the Eastern Conference.

Sports.title: Pierre Sage’s replacement at Lens sacked after four Ligue 1 games due to ‘huge behind the scenes bust-up’
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage’s replacement at Lens sacked after four Ligue 1 games due to ‘huge behind the scenes bust-up’

Lens have reportedly sacked manager Dino Toppmoller after just four league games following a bust-up behind the scenes.

Toppmoller replaced Pierre Sage in the dugout in June after the former boss left his position to join Crystal Palace.

2 Sage has left Lens after his assistant was let go by the Ligue 1 side Credit: AFP

However, his tenure in charge of the club has already come to an end, despite his side winning in three of his six matches.

According to reports in France, Toppmoller has lost his job at Lens after his assistant Nelson Morgado was dismissed.

Morgado had worked with the German since 2017 and was one of his closest connections, having teamed up at Eintracht Frankfurt too.

But the assistant is reported to have been demanding more commitment and passion from the French members of Lens' staff, which made them uncomfortable.

And that led to his exit earlier this week - but following that news, manager Toppmoller has also left the club.

Why have Lens sacked Toppmoller?

Toppmoller is reported to have stood in solidarity for Morgado and found his coach's dismissal unacceptable.

German outlet BILD claims he argued with the club about their direct interference with his team of staff.

That bust-up seems to have led to his sacking, rather than it being anything to do with results.

Lens beat PSG to win the Trophee des Champions at the start of the season and won their Ligue 1 opener 5-2 against Auxerre.

Two league defeats then followed, but they then beat Slavia Prague 3-2 in the Champions League last week, going on to draw away at Le Mans on Sunday.

2 Toppmoller leaves the club with Lens sitting 10th in the league table Credit: Getty

Toppmoller's managerial career

Toppmoller was named Lens manager after Sage left for the Premier League, returning to management after five months away.

He left his previous role at Frankfurt in January after just under three years at the Bundesliga club.

The 45-year-old took charge of 121 games for them, winning 51 in all competitions and taking them to the Champions League.

Before that, Toppmoller hadn't had much of a managerial career, getting the Frankfurt job after working as an assistant to Julian Nagelsmann at RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich.

As a player, he was on Manchester City's books in 2001, but played most of his football in the German lower leagues.

Now, he is going to be on the lookout for another job after seemingly taking a stand that has led to his sacking at Lens.

Sports.title: ‘Absolutely broken’ – Ex-Rangers forward Nacho Novo’s stepson dies aged 26
Sports.content:
Rangers legend Nacho Novo has announced the tragic death of his stepson at the age of 26.

The Spaniard, who now manages Scottish seventh tier outfit Darvel FC, shared the news stepson Ross’s untimely passing in a heart-breaking Instagram post.



3 Novo shared moving images of his time with his late stepson Credit: Instagram @nnovo10

The 47-year-old wrote: "Nothing in my life could’ve prepared me for this post. We are absolutely broken to share the sad news that our beautiful boy has tragically passed away.

"Please respect our family's privacy during this extremely difficult time. Forever in our hearts my boy".

Ross's younger brother posted his own tribute on Tiktok, writing: "U were the best ever.



He continued: "Rest in peace to my big brother. Going to miss you so much. Hope you're okay and safe up there.

“Thanks for always looking after me. I love you so so much, I can't believe it's true. You were the best brother ever. Forever 26."



A statement from Darvel FC read: “The Club’s thoughts are with Nacho and his family at this sad time and we ask that everyone respects the families’ privacy during this extremely difficult time.”

Tributes pour in

Further tributes quickly poured in from fans, media personalities and ex-teammates.



Presenter Laura Woods wrote: "I'm so sorry for your loss Nacho, rest in peace your beautiful boy."

Wrestling star Grado replied: "So sorry to hear this Nacho - absolutely heart breaking. My thoughts are with you and your family."

Ex-Rangers teammate Michael Mols also commented writing: “Unbelievable Nacho. My thoughts and prayers and my condolences.”

3 Novo was inundated with tributes from fans and former teammates following Ross's passing Credit: Instagram @nnovo10



Meanwhile, former Rangers star Steven Davis added: “Thoughts with you all at this difficult time.”

A spokesperson for Rangers FC wrote: "The thoughts of everyone at Rangers are with you at this sad time Nacho."

Ross's cause of death has not yet been disclosed.

Nacho married Ross’s mother Donna Clark in 2015 following a long-term relationship.

The couple share a teenage son and Novo is stepdad to Donna’s sons Ross and Dylan.



The former striker, who netted 70 goals in 250 games for the Gers, retired from football in 2017.

3 Novo helped fire the Ibrox club to three SPL titles

His efforts saw him inducted into the club’s Hall of Fame three years before hanging up his boots.

During his time at Ibrox, Novo won three league titles and three league cups while lifting the Scottish Cup twice.



Aside from his stint at Rangers, he enjoyed spells with Raith Rovers, Dundee and Greenock Morton.

In 2018, he suffered a heart attack while playing for a Rangers legends team in Berlin and underwent emergency surgery to save his life.

Sports.title: Why Man United must win JJ Gabriel battle as Real Madrid, Barcelona and three Premier League clubs circle
Sports.content:
Why Man United must win JJ Gabriel battle as Real Madrid, Barcelona and three Premier League clubs circle

Manchester United have been urged to make a statement by keeping hold of wantaway wonderkid JJ Gabriel.

The Red Devils have been dealt a major blow with the highly-rated 15-year-old asking to leave the club in a shock move.

4 Wonderkid Gabriel has dropped a bombshell and asked to leave Man United Credit: Getty

Recently labelled a 'generational talent' by Man United legend Ryan Giggs, Gabriel has been tipped for a bright future at Old Trafford.

Excitement only grew last week, when the teenager scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut for the Red Devils' U19s.

However, just five days on from his stunning exploits, Gabriel has now sent a formal notice to cancel his registration with the club.

The youngster wants to become a free agent, with Man United unclear on what has prompted the surprise decision.

talkSPORT understands the club are still hopeful of buying enough time to resolve the issue, but that the young star is pushing to leave as soon as possible for a new challenge.

While nothing formal is currently lined up, it's understood Gabriel has interest from Premier League rivals Arsenal, Manchester City and Chelsea - with talkSPORT reporting the latter's last month.

Spanish and German sides are also interested - namely Barcelona and Real Madrid, who have both made pitches for several months, with interested clubs being told Gabriel was unhappy during pre-season.

Premier League rivals keen

talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook discussed the shock news regarding Gabriel with Hawksbee and Jacobs, and he insisted United must do all they can to hold onto the youngster,

He began: "This is not a massive surprise to me…

“The messaging coming out of United was that they were confident of securing his future despite whispers coming from Chelsea.

4 Gabriel has also represented England Under-15s and Under-16s Credit: Getty

"Also, clubs on the continent, Arsenal, Manchester City as well. Now we hear that he's asked to leave…"

Chelsea's interest in Gabriel comes despite the club currently serving a nine-month academy transfer ban for breaching Premier League rules on payments to agents.

However, with the embargo coming into effect in March earlier this year, the Blues have just three months left to serve of this, while it's understood that United are not currently able to de-register Gabriel, who has a contract until next summer.

A move to one of the El Clasico clubs is seen as a viable one for Gabriel.

Crook: Losing Gabriel will spark concern

Crook has insisted it will come as a huge blow to United if Gabriel were to eventually leave for Chelsea - or indeed any of their rivals.

He pointed to the Red Devils' rich history of developing home grown talent, which includes the legendary Class of 92, as well as current first team stars Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo.

4 Gabriel had been tipped to follow in Marcus Rashford's footsteps by becoming a teenage sensation at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

Crook continued: “If he were to leave, it would raise questions again of how the club is being run.

"You look at the history of Man United, the DNA, it's all about the young, homegrown talent bursting into the first team.

"If one of their own decides that his future is better served, particularly somewhere like Chelsea, that's a real kick in the face."

Crook added: “You think not just about the patience of it, but the people around them and how much of this is being led by JJ Gabriel’s advisors, his family, and how much is his own doing.

“What he did do, and this is quite common now, is he deleted all reference of Man United on his social media, so I guess the writing was on the wall when he did that.”

United's transfer market struggles highlighted

Continuing to highlight the importance of keeping Gabriel, Crook insisted United must be able to hold onto their homegrown talent, given their recent struggles in landing top transfer targets.

4 Elliot Anderson chose Man City over United, and played a crucial role in his new side's recent Manchester derby victory Credit: Getty

The Red Devils lost out in the battle to sign Elliot Anderson this summer, who instead joined rivals Manchester City for £116million.

On Gabriel, Crook explained: "I think they feel as if time is on their side. United don't have to accept the request... they have no intention of doing that.

"But clearly, the reason this has happened now is because of the interest from other clubs - Chelsea are certainly one who are keen, Bayern Munich over in Germany too.

“He’s so good that he’s going to have his pick of the teams.

"This is a difficult battle for Man United, but I think optically, it's one that Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS have to win because Man United can't attract top senior players anymore, Elliot Anderson for a prime example.

“If they start losing their best young players to Premier League rivals as well, then I think that's a really bad look for Ratcliffe and the Glazers."

Sports.title: Premier League icon Shaka Hislop delivers health update after prostate cancer diagnosis
Sports.content:
Shaka Hislop has urged more men to be screened for prostate cancer after providing an update on his own battle with the disease.

The former goalkeeper revealed in December that he had been diagnosed with a 'fairly aggressive prostate cancer'.



3 Hislop has provided a health update following his prostate cancer diagnosis Credit: Getty

Hislop had first requested a PSA test during an annual physical exam which prompted a 'radical' prostatectomy in 2024.

However, he was later diagnosed with the disease despite an operation on his prostate gland.

A PSA test is a blood test used to check for prostate conditions.

Hislop provides cancer update

Hislop has now provided an update on his cancer battle, revealing he is 'doing well' but faces a journey across the upcoming years.



The 57-year-old joined Paul Hawksbee and Andy Jacobs live on talkSPORT on Tuesday.

Speaking on Hawksbee & Jacobs, he explained: "I’m doing well. I remain on medication, I will be for the next few years at least.



"But it seems to be, I don’t want to say it’s a remission because it’s still an ongoing process.

"But I had my blood work done just about a month ago and everything is progressing as you’d hope, so I’m happy about that.



"I recognise it’s going to be a little bit of a journey for a few years, but I’m strapped in and ready for it."

Urging other men to go for PSA tests, Hislop added: "Please go and get your PSA checked. It’s absolutely imperative.

3 Hislop urged more men to go for PSA tests as he revealed he is 'doing well' after his diagnosis Credit: Getty

"Without a prostate screening, I would not have caught mine and as I’ve mentioned in my message, mine turned out to be a fairly aggressive cancer.



"Who knows what story I’d be telling right now. So I will also add, I had no history of cancer, let alone prostate cancer, in my family.

"So don’t let that lull you into a false sense of security."

As a player, Hislop made 221 Premier League appearances for West Ham United, Newcastle United and Portsmouth.

He also had spells at both Reading and FC Dallas during his professional career.

The London-born stopper represented Trinidad and Tobago at international level.



3 Hislop made 221 Premier League appearances for West Ham, Newcastle and Portsmouth Credit: Getty

Hislop won 26 caps for the Soca Warriors between 1999 and 2006.

He was also part of their squad for the 2006 World Cup, featuring twice on their only appearance at the finals.

Sports.title: ‘Really disappointing’ – Howard Webb slams ‘tunnel vision’ of officials that missed offside for Man City goal
Sports.content:
Howard Webb has admitted that VAR Matt Donohue missing the offside call in the weekend's Manchester derby was an oversight.

Erling Haaland scored for Manchester City in a 1-0 win at Manchester United on Sunday and the goal was awarded after a lengthy review.

3 City's winning goal against United should not have stood, as per Webb Credit: Sky Sports

The decision to let the goal stand raised eyebrows as midfielder Enzo Fernandez appeared to be in an offside position and interfering with playing, despite him not touching the ball.

A post from the Premier League Match Centre read: "VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.

"The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball."

However, referee governing body Pro Ref later admitted that it was the wrong decision, with VAR Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus not featuring in the next set of Premier League matches.

Pro Ref chief Webb has now addressed what happened and admitted his frustration with the outcome.

VAR had 'tunnel vision'

"I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are," he said on Match Officials Mic'd Up, per the BBC.

"None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation.

"They'll not be officiating again until after the international break."

Webb, a former referee himself, added: "The VAR gets super-focused on Haaland. He establishes he's onside, he thinks that's a good goal.

"He doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez's position. He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score.

3 Webb has revealed his disappointment with the VAR process Credit: Sky Sports

"In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. It's down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn't happen on this occasion.

"What looks like a really clear subjective offside, because Fernandez doesn't touch the ball but still clearly impacts [the play but] doesn't get identified, and it's really disappointing.

"This goal should've been disallowed. And highly unfortunately, it wasn't, and we'll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again."

Pro Ref said they contacted United after the match to 'acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement', and that the incident is set to be reviewed.

Ex-Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher also told talkSPORT on Sunday evening that he 'couldn't believe' offside wasn't given.

The controversy has reignited questions over whether or not VAR should remain in the Premier League.

3 Haaland's goal stood and won the derby for City amid the missed offside Credit: Getty

talkSPORT's Adrian Durham has claimed that it makes referees 'look stupid' and is a 'stain on the game'.

Haaland's goal is one of the most contentious decisions involving VAR since its introduction into the Premier League in the 2019/20 season, with former manager Steve Bruce calling it the 'worst' he has seen.

Arguably the most notable error came in September 2023 when Luis Diaz had a goal wrongly ruled out for offside.

The Liverpool forward scored during the first half of their 2-1 defeat at Tottenham Hotspur and replays showed him in an onside position.

However, a 'significant human error' from the officials meant the goal did not stand, with the PGMOL (Professional Game Match Officials Board) calling it 'a clear and obvious factual error'.

Wolves submitted a proposal calling for the removal of VAR in 2024, but Premier League clubs voted 19-1 to keep it.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel urged to consider uncapped Premier League striker with 32 career goals
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel urged to consider uncapped Premier League striker with 32 career goals

An England team without talismanic captain Harry Kane doesn’t bear thinking about.

However, that notion is closer to becoming a reality that many would like to admit with the striker now at the age of 33.



5 Kane has netted a record 85 goals in 121 games for England Credit: Getty

Much of the trepidation stems from what lies in wait post-Kane... or what doesn’t.

Such is the disparity between Kane’s level and the rest of the pack, each tournament that passes by feels like a missed opportunity at glory for the Three Lions.

The pot of attacking talent waiting in line is thin, however, talkSPORT’s Simon Jordan has urged Three Lions’ head coach Thomas Tuchel to keep a close eye on Liam Delap.



The Nottingham Forest striker opened his account for the club in style during Saturday’s 2-1 win at Aston Villa.

Delap, who endured a frustrating campaign at Chelsea last season, has quickly shown signs of recapturing the kind of form that earned him a £30million switch from Ipswich to Stamford Bridge in 2025.



Quizzed on whether Delap could one day fill the international void left by Kane, Jordan remained open on what the 23-year-old could offer the Three Lions in the future.

Are you watching Tuchel?

“Delap might do it, he’s a good player, “ Jordan said. “He had a great season at Ipswich in a side that could really compete and he scored a few goals.



“He went to Chelsea and got lost in the vacuum.

“That happens to young players. He’s gone to Nottingham Forest, two games in; wallop! He starts scoring goals.”

Delap earned plaudits during his season at Portman Road, netting 12 Premier League goals despite the club’s relegation to the Championship.

5 Delap was all smiles after opening his account for Nottingham Forest

5 Tuchel may soon face the unenviable task of finding a replacement for Kane Credit: Getty



Many expected the striker to kick on at Chelsea last season but a hamstring injury just two weeks into the campaign left him sidelined for two months.

Managerial changes followed by a dislocated shoulder further hampered Delap’s development in west London.

He finished the season – and his spell with the club – with just two goals in 41 appearances across all competitions.

Who is England's second best striker?

Another English striker tipped to fill in for Kane is Leeds United’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin.



The 29-year-old, who has scored four goals in 12 caps for England, was instrumental in his side’s 4-1 thrashing of Newcastle on Monday night.

The ex-Everton striker has found the net three times in six matches this season and Jordan hopes he can continue his good run of form.

5 Calvert-Lewin has made a blistering start to the season with Leeds

5 Just like Delap, Calvert-Lewin has the backing of talkSPORT's Jordan Credit: talkSPORT



Asked if Calvert-Lewin was England's second-best striker behind Kane on current form, Jordan said: “Maybe, I mean he’s always been a good player.

“He had that very good season at Everton and then the injuries took their toll on him and he went to Leeds on a free (transfer).

“He’s having a good moment in time, I’d like to see it being sustained.

“The problem for English football is not whether Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the second to Harry Kane, it’s why we haven't got other players we can choose from.



“Ivan Toney going to Saudi Arabia, predominately has been kept in the England set-up because they don’t have any replacements.

“They don’t have a great litany of forward players that can sit in a role that the aging Harry Kane is going to vacant sooner or later.”

Sports.title: Major Florian Wirtz flaw highlighted as £116.5m Liverpool man linked with surprise exit
Sports.content:
Florian Wirtz lacks the hunger to score goals for Liverpool, which puts him behind a handful of his Premier League rivals.

That's the view of Gabby Agbonlahor, with the German international eyeing a much-improved season amid interest from Bayern Munich.

3 Wirtz continues to lack in goals and assists for Liverpool Credit: Getty

Wirtz made a slow start to life at Liverpool following his £116.5million move from Bayer Leverkusen in June 2025 and later ended his debut campaign with seven goals and ten assists in 49 outings.

A total 17 goal contributions is by no means poor but many fans will have expected more given his price tag, despite him not being able to influence it.

The 23-year-old is yet to score this season but has the opportunity to end his drought in the Carabao Cup third round tonight at Anfield.

Liverpool host a struggling Tottenham Hotspur, live on talkSPORT 2, days after being held to 0-0 draw by Fulham in the Premier League.

Looking ahead to the cup tie against Spurs, former Aston Villa striker Agbonlahor explained on talkSPORT Breakfast what he believes Wirtz lacks in front of goal.

"When you look at his stats... we don't want to go on just stats, but five goals, four assists in 37 Premier League appearances.

He added: "There was a player at Aston Villa, I won't name his name, but he was the best player on the training pitch. In the little five-a-sides, you couldn't get near him, the best player.

"Then when he got onto an 11-a-side pitch, he didn't really do it. I look at him (Wirtz) and say, 'He would definitely be the best player in training, but he seems a bit lightweight'.

"Against Atletico Madrid (in the Champions League, 2-1 win), he was better, he was making some great passes in behind.

"But he needs the hunger to score that Rayan Cherki has got, Cole Palmer has got, Martin Odegaard has now got, Bruno Fernandes.

3 Agbonlahor suggested Wirtz could take a leaf out of the book of the likes of Fernandes, who won the PFA Player of the Year award for last season Credit: Getty

"When you're that number 10... it's a lucky position to play. When I played it at Villa a handful of times, I loved it in there!

"I'd roam around wherever I liked, get on the ball and make things happen. He needs to do a lot more than what he's doing."

Bayern 'keeping an eye' on Wirtz?

Although Wirtz has underwhelmed at Liverpool, recent reports have linked him with German giants Bayern.

A move to the Bundesliga champions would grant him a return to the league in which he made a name for himself as a promising prospect.

Wirtz registered 35 goals and 47 assists across 140 league appearances in the top flight of German football with Leverkusen.

And when assessing the reported Bayern interest, European football journalist Andy Brassell hinted that they could be keen on a move if he continues to falter at Liverpool.

3 Bayern have been credited with transfer interest a year after Wirtz joined Liverpool Credit: Getty

"We've seen moments where he's looked really, really good for them, I thought he was great in the Champions League last week against Atletico," he told talkSPORT on Hawksbee and Jacobs.

"But the thing is, when you cost that much money, people are expecting a lot of bang for their buck pretty quickly.

"He stepped into a situation at Liverpool where he was, sort of, expected to be the new centre point of the team, but Mo Salah was still there.

"Liverpool were a mess last season, and I don't think that was Florian Wirtz's fault. So, it is difficult.

"I would be really surprised if Bayern weren't keeping half an eye on him, to see how the situation decants.

"Because maybe it won't work, I think we have to bear that in mind as a possibility."
