World.title: Eto’o could face Cameroon probe over alleged Russia payment
World.content:
Ex-Chelsea and Barcelona striker Samuel Eto’o faces a probe over allegations of embezzlement in his Cameroon football federation role.

The Association of Amateur Football Clubs of Cameroon (ACFAC) has called for a probe into the Cameroonian Football Federation and its chief Samuel Eto’o following media reports of alleged graft.

Eto’o has been accused of improperly receiving a payment from the Russian Football Union in connection with a friendly match between the two countries in October 2023.

According to ACFAC, the Russian Football Union allegedly violated the terms of its contract with the Cameroonian federation FECAFOOT by transferring around 567,000 euros ($655,000) into a bank account that did not belong to the latter.

The association also announced its intention to file a lawsuit against former Barcelona and Inter Milan striker Eto’o in the Cameroonian courts, as well as a separate legal complaint in Russia against the Russian Football Union.

Last month, Eto’o threw his support behind beleaguered FIFA President Gianni Infantino, saying he “hasn’t done anything wrong” despite facing mounting pressure to step down over a controversial World Cup sell-off plan.

World.title: India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets to seal T20 series
World.content:
Sanju Samson’s half century helps India seal three-match series with wins in first two games.

Share India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets to seal T20 series on social media

Sanju Samson scored 57 off 22 balls as India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets to clinch their three-match T20 series with a match to spare on Tuesday.

Samson hit four sixes and seven fours en route to his first half-century since this year’s T20 World Cup final – where he was named player of the tournament.

His opening partner Abhishek Sharma scored 39 off 19 balls – including four sixes – as the duo amassed 88 off only 38 balls.

India finished with 163-3 in 14.5 overs. It had won the first T20 by seven wickets as well, at the same venue on Sunday.

Afghanistan is playing host in this series, in a unique arrangement, and for the second game running, it finished with an under-par score after India won the toss and opted to field.

All-rounder Nitish Reddy picked 3-24 in three overs as Afghanistan was restricted to 159-8 in 20 overs.

Samson and Sharma set a hectic pace as India raced to 82-0 in the powerplay. Afghanistan used spin in the powerplay as compared to the first game, but to no avail.

Rashid Khan came on after the powerplay, getting the breakthrough in the seventh over, as Sharma was out caught at deep midwicket.

Samson carried on to reach his seventh T20 half-century off 20 balls. Khan picked a second wicket in the seventh over, as Samson holed out to long-off.

But India had powered its way to 100 in 7.1 overs – joint second-quickest for them since 2024.

Skipper Shreyas Iyer was Khan’s third victim, out caught at slip, but Ishan Kishan (38 not out) and Tilak Varma (15 not out) polished off the remaining runs without any bother.



Earlier, put in to bat, Afghanistan made another poor start. Rahmanullah Gurbaz fell for a second consecutive duck, this time to Arshdeep Singh.

Skipper Ibrahim Zadran scored 37 off 33 balls to make sure Afghanistan didn’t lose too many wickets in the powerplay again.

But the “hosts” slid from 59-2 to 100-6 in the middle overs and lost their base as Reddy picked two wickets. Afghanistan only managed to recover thanks to a 48-run partnership off 28 balls between Rashid Khan and Mohammad Nabi.

Khan hit 28 off 16 balls with three fours and a six, while Nabi scored 20 off 14 balls.

World.title: Egypt’s el-Sisi meets MBS, backs Saudi call for secure Red Sea navigation
World.content:
Red Sea disruptions impact Egypt’s economy, with Suez Canal revenues dropping by $7bn in two years.

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi has backed Saudi calls for secure and unhindered navigation in the Red Sea during a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Cairo, according to a statement by the Egyptian presidency.

Sisi met the crown prince, known as MBS, on Tuesday as part of a Saudi delegation that included Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and other senior officials.

The statement affirmed that “relations between Egypt and Saudi Arabia can only be exemplary within the Arab framework, and that the security of Saudi Arabia and the Gulf states is an integral part of Egypt’s national security”, while also emphasising efforts to achieve a sustainable political solution to the Yemen conflict. The Saudi-backed Yemeni government has lost key territories including coastal areas vital for oil shipping to the Iran-aligned Houthis in recent days.

MBS emphasised the importance of secure navigation in both the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Red Sea, according to the Saudi Press Agency.

The visit by Saudi leaders comes as Yemen’s Houthi rebels have captured Mocha port and effectively control the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

Despite Houthi assurances that maritime traffic in the Red Sea will not be affected, Saudi-linked ships have been targeted by the group in recent months.

The sharp decline in Red Sea transit affected Egypt’s economy, which relies heavily on Suez Canal tolls as a key source of foreign currency.

Egypt lost approximately $7bn between 2023 and 2024, or about 60 percent of the Suez Canal’s revenues, according to the Suez Canal Authority.



Despite Egypt’s assurances, the country has so far avoided military action to stop the Houthi disruption of tanker traffic in the Red Sea.

World.title: Police crack down on protests against constitutional change in DR Congo
World.content:
Demonstrations held across country against president’s proposed constitutional changes seeking third term.

Share Police crack down on protests against constitutional change in DR Congo on social media

Protests in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have spurned violent clashes as police cracked down.

Police fired tear gas as hundreds of people protested in the capital Kinshasa on Tuesday against proposed constitutional changes that critics worry could allow President Felix Tshisekedi to seek a ‌third term in power. The political unrest adds to DRC’s struggles as it faces a rapidly spreading Ebola outbreak and ongoing conflict in the east of the country.

At least 10 people were arrested during the confrontations, with demonstrations also taking place in the cities of Lubumbashi – a major mining centre in the southeast of the country – and Uvira, despite restrictions imposed by authorities.

The protests were part of a nationwide day of action called by the “C64” coalition, which was forged by opposition forces in a bid to defeat Tshisekedi’s attempt to change the constitution.

“Many of our activists were unfortunately and arbitrarily arrested,” said Mohamed Eyenga of the Envol opposition party, a senior figure in the C64 coalition, according to the AFP news agency.

“We were taken aback by the large deployment of the army and police to prevent this peaceful demonstration,” he said.

However, the provincial police commander, General Blaise Kilimbalimba, insisted that “peaceful” demonstrators had not been arrested.

Congo’s constitution currently limits presidential terms to two five-year increments.



DRC’s parliament adopted a bill in June allowing constitutional changes to be put to a ⁠referendum, and members of Tshisekedi’s coalition have backed changes that would allow him to remain in office.

Opposition parties and the powerful Catholic Church have condemned the proposal.

The unrest comes three weeks after Tshisekedi announced plans for a national dialogue, bringing together opposition parties, civil society groups and religious leaders.

However, the discussion would exclude the M23 and other rebel groups that control parts of eastern DRC. Fighting over the resource-rich region has persisted for decades, and flared up once more in 2024.

Kinshasa accuses Rwanda of supporting the M23 rebels – an allegation that Kigali denies. Key commitments under a precarious peace process remain unresolved.

Officials from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Rwanda are due to reconvene in Geneva, Switzerland on September 16 and 17 for talks on the implementation of the 2025 Washington Accords.

The conflict has complicated the DRC’s bid to suppress the Ebola outbreak, which is now the world’s worst on record.

The disease has spread across conflict-plagued, remote eastern and northern regions, where armed groups have roamed for decades, the presence of the state is weak, and health infrastructure is largely lacking.

World.title: More than 100,000 displaced as they flee violence in Yemen: UN
World.content:
Share More than 100,000 displaced as they flee violence in Yemen: UN on social media

More than 100,000 people have been forced to flee the conflict in Yemen between the Houthis and forces loyal to the internationally recognised government, according to the United Nations.

The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) said in a statement issued on Tuesday that the rapidly escalating hostilities along Yemen’s western coast have displaced more than 100,000 people inside the country, and forced thousands more to risk the dangerous journey across the Bab al-Mandeb strait to reach Djibouti in search of safety.

The UNHCR statement warned that the violence threatens to trigger a humanitarian crisis, as more people are displaced, pressuring communities with limited resources.

The agency said it requires an estimated $14m in new funding to meet the immediate needs of displaced families inside Yemen, with additional support needed for those arriving in Djibouti.

“Many families fled at short notice with few belongings. Shelter, food, clean water, health care and protection services are among the most urgent needs, as receiving communities and displacement sites become overstretched,” the statement reads.

More than 65,000 registered refugees and asylum seekers inside Yemen, mainly from Somalia and Ethiopia, are also facing risks due to the fighting.

The displacement began when the Iran-aligned Houthis began a rapid advance, seizing control of the entirety of Yemen’s Red Sea coast to cement their grip on Bab al-Mandeb.

The strategic waterway is a critical maritime corridor linking the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and has become an alternative shipping route as the United States’ war against Iran choked the Strait of Hormuz.



Aisha Muhammad, a displaced woman, had to leave her five children in their village near the port city of Mocha when it was overrun by the Houthis last week.

“They are being blocked and shot at, so they are trapped inside their homes. They are cooking only rice, no bread, nothing else. My daughters called me saying they want to join us, but it has become too difficult,” said Muhammad.

Hussein Haydara, a displaced man from Hodeidah, said he was forced to escape suddenly with his family.

“You could barely take your children and the fewest essentials with you,” he said. “We were terrified of the shelling and sniper fire, and you just flee as quickly as you can out of fear for your children and your family.”

UNHCR reports that more than 2,400 people made the journey across the Bab al-Mandeb strait in the past four days. Most arrivals are women, children and older people, it said.

“People are arriving after a difficult sea journey, many exhausted, distressed and carrying what little they could take with them,” Sandrine Desamours, UNHCR’s representative in Djibouti, said.

World.title: Denmark says Russian warship fired flares at military helicopter
World.content:
Denmark has accused a Russian warship of firing two emergency flares at one of its helicopters while it was tracking the vessel in the Baltic Sea.

The Danish government has summoned the Russian ambassador over the incident, which it said happened during a "routine" monitoring operation on Monday.

Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen branded the Russian action "reckless" and said it was designed to "intimidate and divide".

Russia said it would "thoroughly investigate" the incident but accused Danish helicopters of making "dangerous manoeuvres" near Russian warships.

It came on the same day that Nato forces shot down a drone over Lithuania in the latest security scare on the alliance's eastern flank, where tensions remain high amid Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In a statement detailing the incident in the Baltic Sea, the Danish armed forces said: "One of the air force's Fennec helicopters was today fired at with flares during a routine photographic operation of a Russian frigate, which was located in international waters off Gedser."

Of the two flares fired at the helicopter, one passed close to it, the statement added.

The Danish foreign ministry described the incident as "completely unacceptable".

Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen accused Russia of "gradually shifting the boundary for what they consider acceptable behaviour", adding: "That is something we cannot accept."

In a statement, Russian ambassador Vladimir Barbin said Moscow would "thoroughly investigate all the circumstances of the incident" but accused the Danish helicopter of carrying out "provocative actions".

Barbin said this was "not the first time that Danish Air Force helicopters have carried out dangerous manoeuvres near Russian warships".

He said he had complained about a similar incident last year, adding that the latest event showed that "communication problems lie not with the Russian Navy's vessels, but with the Danish side".

Russia's behaviour was "reckless and dangerous," the President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen said in a post on social media.

This incident â together with the drone over Lithuania â was "part of a broader pattern of Russian aggression and provocation against Europe", she added.

Danish Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus told Reuters no attempt to make contact with helicopters had been made by the frigate's crew.

World.title: What weapon could the US have put into space?
World.content:
The announcement by the United States that it has deployed a space weapon in Earth's orbit has raised questions about what weaponry is actually in space, and what role it could play in efforts by great powers to dominate that arena.

Washington has given away little in its announcement. Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said the "on orbit" weapon was necessary to safeguard US forces against hostile enemy action, but gave no details about the weapon's capabilities or when it was put into orbit.

So what could this weapon be, and what is the wider picture like for military developments in space? Who else could have similar weaponry?

Space has been a militarised domain since the start of the space age - in the late 1960s, the Soviet Union deployed weapons up there. The Istrebitel Sputnikov (IS; Satellite Destroyer) programme was made up of satellites that were designed to release projectiles that detonated, releasing shrapnel into the path of another (usually American) satellite.

Nowadays, advanced militaries deploy satellites in space for a range of purposes, including reconnaissance, secure communications, detecting missile launches and providing precise location information for targeted strikes.

As warfare becomes more technologically advanced, analysts expect the use of military hardware in space to increase.

World.title: Suspected sabotage causes major Netherlands rail disruption
World.content:
Parts of the Netherlands, including Amsterdam, were hit by major rail disruption after suspected sabotage to the tracks on Tuesday morning, the country's railway infrastructure operator said.

ProRail said pipes and cables were laid on tracks at multiple locations in the country's centre and north in more than 35 incidents.

It added the acts appeared to be intentional, causing widespread cancellations and delays, with new disruptions occurring in some places after objects had initially been removed.

No suspects or motives have yet been identified. Police said a criminal investigation had been launched.

The operator said the pipes and cables caused its computer systems to believe trains were on the tracks, meaning traffic control was unable to clear the railway.

"Placing materials on the tracks is extremely dangerous and unacceptable, and fortunately, it did not lead to any accidents today," it said.

Speaking earlier, Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten described the incidents as "disruptive and life-threatening".

In one case early on Monday, a train "struck metal" on the track near Steenwijk, in the country's east. ProRail said there was no further damage because the train was not travelling at full speed.

The national public prosecutor's office and the Netherlands' intelligence agency AIVD are investigating the incident alongside police.

Routes to the main international airport, Schiphol, Eindhoven and Utrecht were among those affected on Tuesday. The closure of some level crossings also caused some disruption to roads.

World.title: South African president vows justice as more women's bodies found near Johannesburg
World.content:
On Monday, police said that one of them was Elizabeth Moselakgomo, a runner whose disappearance last week sparked a frantic and public search for her.

President Ramaphosa said he had directed that the cases be prioritised: "Our law enforcement agencies are working urgently to establish the facts, keep communities safe and bring the perpetrator or perpetrators to justice."

South Africa experiences some of the world's highest levels of gender-based violence (GBV), with the rate at which women are killed five times higher than the global average, according to UN Women.

The discoveries of the bodies have sparked outrage and fear across the country, with many criticising the authorities for failing to adequately protect women.

Moselakgomo was identified by her relatives on Monday after her body was discovered on Saturday. It was the 38-year-old's young daughter who raised the alarm about her disappearance after she failed to return from her daily run last Wednesday.

The body of the first woman was found in mid-July, the second in late August - the others were discovered this month, two in the last two days.

On Tuesday, police said that the body of woman found on 7 September in a town nearby Kempton Park was also being included - bringing the total number of bodies being investigated to seven.

"After noticing that there are bodies being picked up, we went back to our police stationsâ¦ and unfortunately it came to light that a body of a female in her late 20s was observed in a river next to a mall," Maj-Gen Fred Kekana, acting police chief for Gauteng province, said at a briefing.

Police have urged women in the Kempton Park area - which is by South Africa's main international airport - to avoid walking or running alone "particularly in isolated areas".

South Africa's Commission for Gender Equality urged residents of Kempton Park to work with the police to find the perpetrators.

"These deaths are indicative that women in South Africa continue to face environments in which their ordinary freedom of movement can become a matter of life and death," it said.

"Women should be able to run, walk to work, use public transport, return home, visit friends and participate in community life without having to calculate whether an ordinary activity could place their lives at risk."

World.title: Two sailors missing after tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz, Oman says
World.content:
Two sailors are missing and 23 others have been rescued following an attack on an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, Oman says.

Oman's Maritime Security Centre said the Panama-flagged El Gaia was being towed to an Omani port on Tuesday after a fire broke out in its engine room, adding that the vessel was targeted 1.3 nautical miles (2.4km) north of the Musandam peninsula.

On Monday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the tanker hit naval mines and caught fire while passing through what they described as a restricted and unsafe route.

But the US military insisted the Iranian report was false. It said the tanker was struck by an Iranian missile last month and again by a drone over the weekend.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre, meanwhile, said it had received a report of a fire breaking out on board a vessel that was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of Sunday.

Earlier this month, Iran made a similar claim about an incident that killed two Filipino sailors on a Saudi-owned oil supertanker in the crucial waterway.

The Revolutionary Guards said the vessel, Sidr, caught fire after hitting a naval mine. But Saudi authorities said it was targeted by Iran and maritime security firms reported that it was hit by projectiles north of Musandam.

The International Maritime Organization says at least 22 seafarers have been killed in 79 confirmed incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and the rest of the Middle East since the start of the US and Israel's war with Iran at the end of February.

Also on Tuesday, Iran's semi-official Fars news agency reported that "enemy drones" had targeted two fishing boats in the strait overnight near the Iranian port of Kargan, about 80km (50 miles) north-east of Musandam.

Fars, which is linked to the Revolutionary Guards, cited the deputy governor of Hormozgan province as saying that several fishermen were reported missing following the incident and that a search-and-rescue operation was under way.

Later, a spokesman for the US military's Central Command (Centcom) told the news website Axios that its forces had destroyed two boats which tried to steal a sea drone.

"Iranian small boats recently attempted to take possession of a US unmanned surface vessel, but they were unsuccessful after Centcom forcefully responded," Capt Tim Hawkins said.

The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, has effectively been closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after the Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran has insisted it will not give up some measure of control over the waterway and has targeted vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.

World.title: Iran war has led to US munitions shortfalls, Pentagon inspector confirms
World.content:
The US defence department's inspector general says the war with Iran has led to "shortfalls" in munitions and a bottleneck in resupply, contradicting President Donald Trump who has repeatly denied the US is facing shortages.

Trump has claimed US munitions supplies are "virtually unlimited" and said reporting otherwise is "fake news".

But the independent watchdog said the US spent more than $22 billion on munitions from February through June, leading to "strategic inventory shortfalls".

The BBC has contacted the White House for comment about the discrepancy.

The new report provides a first-of-its-kind, independent glimpse into US weapons stockpiles, data that is typically classified.

Previous estimates have painted a dire picture of the US shortages.

Over the course of the war, US forces have expended vast quantities of both long-range ground attack systems and the air and missile defences used to intercept incoming Iranian attacks.

A late July estimate from the Center for Strategic and International Studies, or CSIS, found that stocks of some interceptors - such as the Patriot missile and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense, or THAAD - were significantly depleted, in some cases by more than half.

The inspector general's report did not disclose exactly how many of the weapons remain.

It did, however, note the inventory shortfalls and reveal "industrial base bottlenecks" for munitions resupply.

The report added that the defence department is now working to "streamline procurement processes and production lead times" to address the shortages and "respond rapidly to a contingency".

Trump and other administration officials have sought to cast reports of shortages as false and "treasonous".

In a 4 August X post, for example, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth described news reporting on the shortages as "not true".

And in a lengthy Truth Social post on 3 September, Trump claimed that the US had "virtually unlimited" amounts of ammunition and is "stockpiling and preparing for any contingency that could happen".

The watchdog's report also notes that equipment losses have totaled $3.7bn, with other $7.4bn in other expenditures. Overall, the US spent $33.4bn (Â£24.7bn) on the war from 28 Feb to 30 Jun.

A separate estimate released on Tuesday by the Congressional Budget Office put the total cost of the war at higher at $38bn, which includes replaced expended munitions and equipment lost in battle, increased flying hours and greater fuel costs.

Among the losses have been four F-15e fighter jets, a highly advanced F-35 Joint Strike Fighter and 30 MQ-9 drones destroyed in "various circumstances".

When US and Israeli strikes began, Trump repeatedly said that the conflict would be over within weeks.

More recently, he said the conflict might not end until "right after" the November midterm elections in the US.

Polls show that the war is unpopular among Americans.

One Reuters/Ipsos poll released in early September found that only 23% of Americans - and only half of Republicans - believe the US to be in a stronger position with Iran compared with before hostilities broke out.

World.title: Canada is a 'safe harbour' for global finance, Carney says
World.content:
Prime Minister Mark Carney is pitching Canada as a "safe harbour" for some of the world's largest investors in an era of geopolitical and economic uncertainty.

Canada is "perfectly situated to build in the new global economic order", he told more than 100 major investors being courted by Ottawa on Tuesday.

Carney has pledged to bring in C$1tn in investments in the ânext â five years as he seeks to reduce Canada's reliance on the US, and the summit this week is a test of whether he can deliver on promises to strengthen economic resilience.

His aim is to have the group, representing more than C$120tn ($86tn; Â£64tn) of assets, invest in sectors like defence, energy, mining, AI and infrastructure.

More than 160 projects, from mines to data centres and pipelines, are on offer.

As its tariffs war with the US grows, Canada is seeking deeper economic partnerships with Europe, Asia and the Middle East and Carney has worked to raise its global profile.

Many of the business leaders attending the Toronto event received personal invitations from the prime minister, who worked in the top tiers of global finance and was a central banker before turning to politics.

"Our goal is simple: to make Canada the most attractive place in the G7 to invest," Carney said on Tuesday morning.

As part of that move, Carney announced plans to privatise operations for four of the country's largest airports, saying it would raise billions of dollars that could be reinvested in transport infrastructure.

Many developed countries allow some degree of private investment in airports, but Canada has lagged behind and its airports operate under a not-for-profit governance model.

The federal government will retain ownership of the underlying land and assets but allow private investments into airport operations, said Carney.

Labour unions have criticised the proposal, saying it will be bad for both workers and passengers.

Much of the action will take place in private sessions and bilateral meetings over the course of the day.

There will, however, be panels with speakers including Deutsche Bank AG CEO Christian Sewing, Bombardier executive Eric Martel, and BlackRock CEO Larry Fink and Blackstone president Jon Gray.

World.title: Nigeria arrests alleged Mexican drug kingpin at international airport
World.content:
An alleged Mexican drug kingpin was arrested in Nigeria last month as he tried to leave the country, the drug enforcement authority has just revealed.

That arrest resulted in the discovery of a suspected industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory - the third such find allegedly linked to Mexicans in four months.

When Arturo Carrera Loaiza, 40, was detained at Lagos international airport, officials allegedly found digital images of him wearing what they believed to be a laboratory coat alongside equipment consistent with meth production.

The pictures' location data led officers to a property in Ebonyi state, where they said chemicals and drug-making equipment were found.

Loaiza has denied involvement in methamphetamine production and said he had been invited to Nigeria by a local contact for a restaurant business venture, according to a statement from the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA).

World.title: Pentagon report reveals Iran war depleted US ammunition stockpile
World.content:
A new Pentagon report has shown that the US is running low on its ammunition stockpile due to its ongoing war with Iran.

The Department of Defence Inspector General report was submitted to the US Congress on Monday, according to the Washington Post.

It accounts for the losses Washington has incurred since the first strike in February. It is one of the first public accounts from any government agency detailing the cost, scope, and scale of the war on the military, the State Department, and other agencies.

Contrary to President Donald Trump’s claim that the US has unlimited weapons and was producing even more exquisite ones, the report stated that Washington was running short.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to the report, the US has suffered significant losses to its munition stockpile, particularly missiles and air-defence interceptors, since the war with Iran began on February 28.

The cost of the war with Iran was estimated to be around $33.4 billion. This does not include the cost of repairing damaged facilities.

Around $22.3 billion was also spent on munitions, according to the report. The report also cited $3.7 billion in equipment losses and $7.4 billion in other expenses.

The report also confirmed that hundreds of buildings and structures used by the US were damaged or destroyed by Iranian attacks, according to Al Jazeera.

Iran also targeted Washington’s Navy’s main logistics hub in the region, in Bahrain, with drones and ballistic missiles.

The US also lost dozens of aircraft, according to the report. It reported the destruction of four F-15E jet fighters, an F-35A Joint Strike Fighter, and an A-10 Warthog, which was also destroyed.

The report stated that twelve KC-135 refuelers and nine other aircraft were also destroyed. More than 30 MQ-9 drones had also been destroyed as of June.

According to the report, the State Department sustained more than $208 million in damage in four countries — Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. That includes $184 million in damages to “diplomatic facilities” and $25 million more due to delays in construction projects.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the first American casualties were recorded in March after three US fighter jets crashed in Kuwait. Three American soldiers died in the crash, with four others seriously injured. Hours later, another US soldier was killed by Iranian missiles.

However, the Pentagon report put the death toll at 18. It said at least 11 personnel were “killed in action”, while seven died in “non-hostile events” during the war.

However, the report did not provide any information on the strike which killed over 165 elementary school girls in Tehran.

This paper reported the US strike at an elementary school in Minab, the Hormozgan province of Southern Iran in February. Five pupils were initially reported dead, before the toll began to rise steadily as emergency workers cleared the wreckage and identified more victims.

This paper also reported that the toll first rose to 95, and then to 118 before rising to over 160 in days.

In March, the Pentagon announced that it had launched a formal investigation into the attack. Then, in June, NBC reported that some senior US military officials said the investigation was in its final stages and that the Pentagon was preparing to share it with lawmakers.

World.title: Roving Heights to host reading for PT Books’ latest title
World.content:
A reading, signing and interactive conversation on PT Books recently published The Muslim Public Servant in Nigeria: Integrity, Justice and the Sacred Trust of Office is scheduled to hold between 4. p.m. and 6 p.m. on Thursday, 17 September at Roving Heights Book Store, City Centre Mall, Abuja.

Written by the notable anticorruption advocate and public intellectual, Umar Yakubu, the book leverages enduring and transcendental Islamic principles as the ethical frame for engaging with the challenges of service, leadership and followership in the country – more so at the public level, which impacts the most across society.

The book examines what it means to serve humanity – and no less Nigeria – with integrity, competence, justice, and accountability.

While tackling systemic issues, with Nigeria as a peculiar point of reference, even as its lessons reverberate through much of the human experience, the book speaks to concerns around corruption, abuse of office, nepotism, incompetence, and the misuse of public resources.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

At the core of the book is the Islamic concept of amanah or trust, which presents public office as a moral responsibility that needs to be discharged for the utmost good of citizens and upliftment of society, contrary to pervasive and perverse manifestation in the privatisation of public resources and goods by a privileged few with access. It is essentially about the recovery of integrity in public affairs as a necessity, which in itself is a crucial act of worship of the Almighty.

In making a case for the recovery of integrity through the rebuilding of trust in society, Mr Yakubu examines the realities of public service in Nigeria, which have evinced the key pathology of corruption/self-seeking, that has equally spawned a malicious entourage comprising incompetence, nepotism, tribalism, conflicts of interest, and the misuse of public resources, alongside disorders including vote buying, etc.

These are ills requiring collective exorcism, the procedure to which the book eloquently lays out. A vital aspect of this retraces the process of selection of the public servant, who needs to be entrusted with social responsibilities only on the basis of competence and trustworthiness, rather than political affiliations, loyalty to patronage networks, or personal relationships.

As an essential manual of The Integrity Arm or the fourth dimension of Governance, The Muslim Public Servant in Nigeria: Integrity, Justice and the Sacred Trust of Office invokes interesting notions among which is “divine laundering,” pertaining to the acts of some located within the juicy entrails of public service, who give back some of their loot to religious causes, towards the purported end of cleaning this up or deflecting the consequences of scavenging the commonwealth.

More so, the author draws a clear line between the performative rituals of religiosity and true ethical conduct, rooted in honesty and fairness in handling the public trust, which is the genuinely acceptable trajectory.

As alluded to, this book outlines universalisable principles, making the Islamic frame deployed a metaphor for the quest for integrity and justice. It’s vital message extends beyond an appeal to only Muslims, whilst the values espoused, such as justice, honesty, competence, accountability, and service are relevant to all interested in building better institutions and a better society.

Overall, The Muslim Public Servant in Nigeria is more than a discussion of Muslims in public office. It is a broader call to a rethinking and recovery of the sacred purpose of power, leadership, responsibility, and service. Its central message is clear: public office is a sacred trust, and those entrusted with it must be prepared to account for how they use that trust.

The Thursday, 17 September reading at Roving Heights Book Store with Dr Umar Yakubu, the Executive Director of Center for Fiscal Transparency and Public Integrity, will have in attendance key organisational actors, civil society leaders, policy experts, other authors, and members of the public. The associated conversation will be moderated by Malam Hanafi Mujeli, during which critical questions around accountability, ethics, and leadership in public service will be explored.

The book, now available across major bookstores in Abuja, Lagos, Ibadan, Kano, and Kaduna, will be signed for those interested in questions of anticorruption, integrity and national recovery at the event.

World.title: Shettima to attend Governor AbdulRazaq’s turbaning as Sardauna of Ilorin
World.content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima is scheduled to be in attendance on Wednesday as Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq is turbanned as Sardauna of Ilorin Emirate at the state capital.

The capital city is alr3ady bustling with activities across the metropolis.

Billboards, banners, and influx of guests from the airport and major highways into the town have been observed in various parks.

Governor AbdulRazaq will be turbaned by the Emir of Ilorin, Ibrahim Sulu-Gambari, at the palace at 1 p.m.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr AbdulRazaq will become the first person to hold the title, which makes him the Defence Minister of Ilorin Emirate.

Vice President Shettima is expected to lead top dignitaries to the event, including state governors, ministers, and lawmakers from across Nigeria.

Meanwhile, the Kwara State Government said it will commission two flagship projects as part of the activities during the state event.

The Vice president will inaugurate the Kwara Garment Factory during his visit.

According to the Senior Special Assistant to Governor on Communications, Ibraheem Abdullateef, the factory can employ over 4000 workers at full capacity, while over 500 staff are currently employed for the official takeoff phase.

Mr Shettima will also commission the multi-storey Revenue House of the Kwara State Internal Revenue Service (KWIRS).

Ahead of the turbanning, the Emir of Ilorin’s palace has worn a new look following renovation over the week.

Freshly painted, the palace is adorning banners of different community associations, political groups, and stakeholders.

Earlier during the announcement in August 2024, the emir said he bestowed Mr AbdulRazaq with the title in recognition of his achievement as state governor and his contributions to the growth and development of the Ilorin Emirate.

World.title: Awoniyi hits another milestone, graduates from PFA Business School
World.content:
Super Eagles striker Taiwo Awoniyi has added another milestone to his career after graduating from the PFA Business School with a Postgraduate Diploma in Global Football Sport Directorship.

Awoniyi, 29, announced the achievement on his Facebook page on Tuesday, describing it as another proud moment away from football.

“Another proud moment for me off the pitch. 🎓

Graduated from the PFA Business School with a Postgraduate Diploma in Global Football Sport Directorship with Merit.

I have always believed that being a footballer shouldn’t stop you from being a student of the game, and education has become an important part of that journey for me.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Thank you to everyone at the PFA Business School, the lecturers and my colleagues, with whom I had the opportunity to learn alongside.

And a special thank you to my family and friends for their encouragement and support throughout.

Still playing and still learning. The journey continues. 🎓🙏🏾”

The qualification adds to Awoniyi’s development beyond the pitch as he continues his professional career with Premier League newcomers Coventry City.

The PFA Business School, an educational initiative of the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA), offers current and former players opportunities to prepare for careers in football management and leadership.

Its Postgraduate Diploma in Global Football Sport Directorship is designed to provide specialised training in areas such as football operations, sporting strategy, management, and the role of the modern sporting director. The programme is delivered part-time over two academic years, with the qualification awarded by the University of Portsmouth in collaboration with the PFA Business School.

Following a growing trend

Awoniyi’s achievement places him among some prominent footballers who have pursued higher education while playing at the highest level.

Former Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany graduated with a Master’s in Business Administration from Alliance Manchester Business School in 2017. He completed the part-time Global MBA while playing and was awarded a merit grade, with his dissertation examining how Premier League clubs could benefit from home advantage.

Italian defender Giorgio Chiellini also combined professional football with academic studies. He earned a bachelor’s degree in Economics and Commerce from the University of Turin in 2010, then completed a Master’s in Business Administration in 2017, graduating cum laude. His master’s thesis examined Juventus’ business model in an international context.

For Awoniyi, the latest qualification comes at a significant stage of his playing career.

Red card overshadows weekend

Just two days before announcing his academic achievement, Awoniyi experienced a difficult afternoon on the pitch as Coventry suffered a 5-0 home defeat to Brighton in the Premier League.

The Nigerian striker was sent off in the 53rd minute after catching Brighton defender Maxim De Cuyper with his arm during an aerial challenge. The dismissal was Awoniyi’s first Premier League red card and second career sending-off.

It was his 94th Premier League appearance, and his fourth league appearance for Coventry this season.

Despite the setback on the pitch, Awoniyi’s latest qualification underlines his effort to prepare for life beyond his playing career.

World.title: Rainbow Coalition: Wike taunts APC governors, says he never promised PDP won’t field candidates
World.content:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has taunted governors elected on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC) over their opposition to the Rainbow Coalition he is promoting to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

Mr Wike, a leader of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and a member of the APC-led federal government, challenged the governors to focus on campaigning for Mr Tinubu rather than intervening in the coalition.

The minister clarified in a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, in response to the APC Governors Forum’s position on the coalition.

PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that the APC Governors Forum, chaired by Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, opposed any political coalition or alliance that could threaten the party and its candidates’ chances in the 2027 elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Uzodimma, who is also the secretary of the Tinubu Campaign Council, argued that aligning with such a political arrangement could undermine Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid and weaken the APC ahead of the elections.

Some APC leaders had earlier expressed concerns about the coalition, particularly following allegations that Mr Wike was using the platform to support politicians who lost the APC primaries and are now contesting elections on the PDP platform.

Wike taunts Uzodimma

Mr Wike took a swipe at Mr Uzodimma over his emergence as governor of Imo State after the 2019 governorship election, in which he initially placed fourth before the Supreme Court declared him the winner in 2020.

The minister said Nigerian politics had moved beyond relying on court declarations and should now focus on grassroots mobilisation and winning votes at polling units.

Although Mr Uzodimma’s name was not mentioned in the statement, the remark was apparently directed at the Imo governor.

“The minister said politics is no longer about coming from fourth position to be governor, it is about genuinely mobilising support and winning elections from the polling units,” he said.

‘Can APC governors deliver Tinubu’s votes?’

Mr Wike also questioned Mr Uzodimma’s ability to deliver Imo State for Mr Tinubu in 2027, citing the state’s voting patterns in the 2023 presidential and National Assembly elections.

He noted that whereas APC candidates won two senatorial seats in Imo State in 2023, Mr Tinubu secured less than 15 per cent of the presidential votes cast in the state.

“In Imo State under Governor Hope Uzodinma, how did APC win two senate seats in 2023, in an election held the same day as that of the President, and APC had less than 15 per cent in the presidential election? Was it a rainbow coalition? Were the voters confused?” he asked.

Mr Wike extended his criticism to the governors of Ebonyi, Abia and Enugu states, where Mr Tinubu also performed poorly in the 2023 presidential election despite APC candidates winning some National Assembly seats.

“Was it the Rainbow Coalition that also made the APC to win the National Assembly elections in Ebonyi, Abia, and Enugu, where the President did not have 10 per cent of the votes?

“If in 2023, the voters in Imo, Abia, Enugu, and Ebonyi voted APC in the Senatorial election and voted another party in the presidential election, they won’t be confused in 2027, provided we all support the president genuinely this time,” he said.

Mr Wike urged the governors to pay greater attention to Mr Tinubu’s re-election campaign than they did to his 2023 campaign.

“After the President has been reelected, we can all go and face elections in our states.”

I never promised PDP won’t field candidates

Responding to allegations that he was using the coalition to support politicians against the APC, Mr Wike said he had never promised that the PDP would not field candidates in the 2027 elections.

“What I said and stand for is that I will mobilise support for the reelection of the President. I never promised anyone that PDP would not field candidates to contest the governorship, National Assembly, and House of Assembly elections.

“Most importantly, the Rainbow Coalition has nothing to do with the APC. Rather, it is their own way of mobilising support across political parties for Mr President, who has done well to deserve a second term,” the minister stated.

Mr Wike is backing the PDP group led by Abdulrahman Mohammed. The group is recognised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to which it submitted its list of candidates.

It is also presenting Sandy Onor, a former senator, as its presidential candidate in the 16 January election, though the minister said he supports President Tinubu.

A faction of the PDP led by Kabiru Turaki, a former minister of special duties and senior lawyer, still claims to be the party’s authentic group.

The faction had attempted to present former President Goodluck Jonathan as its presidential candidate in the 2027 poll.

World.title: Police arrest kidnap suspects while collecting N1.5m ransom in Ondo, rescue victims
World.content:
The Ondo State Police Command says it has arrested three persons suspected to be kidnappers after they emerged from the forest to collect ransom for their victims.

Besides the arrest of the suspects, the two kidnapped victims were rescued during an operation.

The ransom amounting to N1.5 million, a motor bike and foodstuffs were also recovered from the suspects by the police.

A statement on Tuesday by the command’s spokesperson, Abayomi Jimoh, said the suspects were arrested in Isua-Akoko area of the state.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The operation commenced on Friday, September 11, 2026, following credible intelligence that a group of suspected kidnappers hibernating in the thick forest along the Ifira–Idoani axis were planning to emerge from their hideout to collect ransom,” the statement read.

“Acting on the intelligence, operatives of Isua Division, in collaboration with personnel of the Ondo State Security Network (Amotekun) and Agbe-Koya, embarked on a coordinated rescue and ambush operation deep inside the forest.

“The security operatives strategically positioned themselves along the suspected route and maintained surveillance for several hours. At about 2330 hours, the suspected kidnappers, numbering about four and armed with firearms, emerged from the forest. On sighting the security operatives, they opened fire, prompting the security team to tactically repel the attack and rescue the two victims, Mr. Owolabi Patrick and Asoto Dada, unhurt.

“During the encounter, the security operatives recovered the sum of ₦1,500,000 (One Million, Five Hundred Thousand Naira), suspected to have been brought for ransom payment. The suspected kidnappers sustained gunshot injuries and escaped into the thick forest.”

Mr Jimoh said a sustained follow-up operations and credible intelligence on Sunday, 13 September led to the arrest of three of rhe suspects who were sighted along the Idoani Road.

He said operatives immediately mobilised to the area, resulting in the arrest of three suspects, while two of them had sustained gunshot injuries to their legs.

“The arrested suspects are: Abdullahi Abubakar, male, Ibrahim Abubakar, male, and Oseni Abubakar, male, all resident of Akunnu area. The two rescued victims, subsequently came to the Police Station and positively identified the arrested suspects as the persons who abducted them,” Mr Jimoh said.

“A Bajaj motorcycle earlier recovered by the Police has also been identified by the victims as being connected to the criminal operation. The motorcycle remains in Police custody as part of the ongoing investigation.”

Mr Jimoh said the Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, commended the officers and men of Isua Division, alongside personnel of Amotekun and Agbe-Koya, for their courage, professionalism and effective collaboration, which contributed to the successful rescue of the victims and subsequent arrest of the suspects.

He said the CP immediately ordered that the case be transferred to the Special Anti-Kidnapping Squad, Akure, for discreet investigation, with a view to uncovering the full network and bringing all those connected with the criminal operation to justice.

“The Command reiterates its determination to deny criminal elements access to forests and other hideouts within the State and will continue to sustain intelligence-led operations against kidnappers and other criminal elements,” Mr Jimoh added.

The Amotekun regularly parades suspected criminals across the 18 local government areas, including rings of kidnappers operating in regions like Ore, Akoko, and major highways.

Only last week the agency paraded three suspected kidnappers who dressed in army uniforms to deceive their victims.

The Commander of the Security Network, Adetunji Adeleye, said the suspected kidnappers were arrested in Akure North Local Government Area of the state by a combined team of Fulani farmers and local vigilantes.

World.title: 2027: Nigerians react to bishops’ endorsement of Tinubu’s re-election bid
World.content:
Some Nigerians have reacted to the Charismatic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria’s recent endorsement of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in the 2027 general election.

President Tinubu, who will complete his first four-year term in office on 29 May, is seeking re-election on the All Progressives Congress (APC) platform in the 16 January presidential election.

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) recently cleared the president and 17 other candidates from other political parties for the election.

Rising from the 2026 Synod Charismatics Bishop Conference of Nigeria and International Communion of Charismatic Archbishops, Bishops and Apostles (ICCABA), held at the National Christian Centre, Abuja, last Sunday, the archbishops declared support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election, citing the president’s support for the Christian faith through appointments and endorsement of state governors, who are of the faith.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The president did not only appoint at the national level, but he also supported the emergence of Christian governors to be the majority in Nigeria. He has stood with Christianity alongside his wife.

“We stand with the president today and as long as he’s willing to be our president and even come in 2027, we will be standing with him. On this, this house has endorsed him for the 2027 presidency,” Leonard Kawas, an archbishop and CBCN president general, said during the grand finale of the synod.

The conference brought together Christian leaders to deliberate on peace, national unity, religious freedom, security, good governance and the role of the church in national development.

The Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), George Akume, represented Mr Tinubu at the event.

However, the Christian leaders’ endorsement of President Tinubu has sparked criticism from some Nigerians, who said they should be apolitical, while others described them as fake.

Criticisms

In a press statement, Elijah Ayodele, a primate and leader of the Inry Evangelical Spiritual Church, contended that the bishops who endorsed President Tinubu for a second term were not driven by divine sanction but by hunger for appointment or the need to be close to the seat of power.

In the statement signed by his media aide, the cleric cautioned the president not to be overjoyed by the endorsement, dismissing it as fake.

A Catholic priest with the username @Frjames on X also said, “It’s not God that led you – money did!”

Human Rights activist and lawyer, Deji Adeyanju, commented on the viral video on X, saying, “Religious leaders have a duty to respect the sanctity of their institutions and must not allow themselves to be used as a political tool.”

Another X user with the username @Sports_Doctor2 said that the statement made by Mr Kawas stemmed from his controversy with the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi.

“His problem with Peter Obi is not that he’s not credible; it’s because he refused to pay him for supporting him. This shows you he’s being paid to support whoever he’s supporting now,” the X user stated.

The supporters

However, other Nigerians applauded the religious leader’s action.

Lere Olayinka, spokesperson for the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, said the criticism against Mr Kawas came because he stopped supporting Mr Obi.

“He wasn’t a fake bishop; he became a fake bishop when he stopped supporting their ‘fake man.’ Bishop Kawas is facing what everyone who is not supporting Peter Obi is facing.”

Another user on YouTube with the username @Portablesminary-kg5wq said, “The charismatic has spoken. If you don’t believe them because of your candidate, then that is your problem. You would have felt better if they had chosen your candidate. What a hypocrite!”

Echoes from the past

In 2022, during the official unveiling of Kashim Shettima, as running mate to the All-Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate in Abuja, some Christian clerics were in attendance, stirring controversy over their authenticity and suspicion around the event.

Some Christian groups interpreted the appearance of the clerics as an attempt to validate the Muslim-Muslim ticket.

President Tinubu and Mr Shettima are both Muslims.

Some Christian associations opposed the choice of a Muslim/Muslim ticket, describing it as part of the “Islamisation agenda” by the ruling party.

Archbishops defend action

Meanwhile, days after the Synod, Mr Kawas and the conference Secretary General, Chivir Chianson, came out to defend the endorsement of Mr Tinubu for a second term.

In an interview on ARISE TV on Saturday, the archbishop responded to critics, saying they are not fake.

“For those who say we are fake bishops, I didn’t just become a bishop today. I’ve been a bishop for over 25 years; I’ve been an archbishop for 14 years. My archbishopric is internationally recognised because I live in Washington DC,” Mr Kawas, who leads the Abuja-based World Harvest Ministries, said.

He also addressed critics who cited his strife with Mr Obi.

He said, “People call me fake, yet I supported Peter Obi at the initial stage of his presidential ambition and went with him everywhere in Nigeria, and he never gave me N1. Neither did he ever ask me how I came to the campaign; he would just see me there. We came and supported him. He never asked where I slept. Yet I did it, and nobody called me fake.”

He stated further, “It is unheard of for anybody to think that just because I am a bishop, I should have no interest in politics. God requires us to understand that He told us right from Genesis when He created man in verse 26, that the first assignment given to a man was to have dominion in this world. To have dominion means to be in charge. The Bible says when the righteous rule, the people rejoice. It is very painful that Christians have sat back, folded their hands, and said politics is a dirty game.”

Mr Kawas added that the concerns he once held over the Muslim-Muslim ticket have since been clarified, proving that it is not a leader’s religion that matters, but the quality of their leadership.

“I will hold nothing back when telling the president the truth; we were the ones that called on him to look into the matter when people were dying en masse in Benue State,” he stated.

Also, replying to the leader of the Inry Evangelical Spiritual church, he said, “I am seriously disappointed at Primate Elijah; he should have known better,”.

On his part, Mr Chianson said the position of the clerics stemmed from the policies and development achieved by Tinubu’s administration in the first term.

“Nigeria has been doing a lot better, especially in 2026 under his watch; our GDP has been growing. Now the unemployment rate has dropped as well. Unlike the previous government, diversity was badly mismanaged. Now he has restored our hopes, especially those of us from the Christian community,” he said in the interview with Arise Television.

Mr Chianson further pointed to the appointment of Mr Akume as SGF as a major turning point.

He argued that, upon closer examination of key ministries, the administration had ensured every ethnic group was represented in sensitive appointments, unlike the previous government, under which a single ethnic group had dominated such roles.

“He (Tinubu) will win, and he’s not only going to win; he will perform even better,” Mr Chianson said.

World.title: Gates Foundation commits $1 billion to expand equitable AI access
World.content:
The Gates Foundation has announced plans to spend at least $1 billion over the next two years to expand access to artificial intelligence and AI-enabled solutions, particularly for communities with limited access to technology.

The foundation announced this in a press release on Tuesday as it launched its 10th annual Goalkeepers Report.

The report titled: Make This Matter: AI, Equity, and the Choice We Can’t Delay “focuses on the urgent actions needed to ensure that AI helps narrow gaps between the richest and poorest rather than widening them.

“The report includes examples of foundation-supported partners that are already changing lives using AI in clinics and classrooms and on small farms,” the foundation noted.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Funding areas

The foundation said 40 per cent of the funding will go towards education, including AI tutoring to individualise student learning and d teaching tools in the United States and other countries.

Another 40 per cent will support healthcare, including AI tools for diagnostics and clinical decision-making by frontline health workers, maternal and newborn care, and the discovery of new drugs and vaccines.

Agriculture will receive 10 per cent of the funding, including support for AI-generated advice for smallholder farmers based on their soil, weather and crop conditions.

The remaining 10 per cent will support the digital foundation needed for equitable AI, including datasets in languages that existing AI tools do not yet understand.

The foundation said equitable access to AI would require deliberate action from governments, technology companies, philanthropy and communities.

Language gap

The report also highlights the under-representation of many languages in the data used to develop AI systems.

According to the foundation, more than 90 per cent of the data used to train early large language models came from English-language sources.

It said this has left many communities that could benefit from AI poorly represented in the data on which the tools were built.

The foundation recommended developing AI tools that work in the languages people speak and using data and expertise from the communities where the tools will be deployed.

It noted that the report also calls for countries and communities to have a greater role in determining how data used for AI is managed and protected.

It said doctors, farmers, teachers and developers need opportunities to learn how to assess AI tools and adapt them to their local settings.

The foundation also said affordable access to AI technology would require action from technology companies, as well as investment from governments and philanthropic organisations.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident,” Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation, once was quoted to have said.

Mr Gates called on government leaders and the companies developing the technology to measure success not only by what AI can do for the most profitable users but by what it can do for the people who stand the most to gain.”

World.title: 2027: Ex-Nasarawa Speaker begs defectors to return to APC
World.content:
The immediate past Speaker, Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Alhaji Ibrahim Balarabe, has appealed to all aggrieved members who defected from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to other parties to return to the party.

He said the appeal became imperative in view of the fact that they laboured to build a house, only to vacate it “at the time you need it most.”

The former speaker made the call in an interview with newsmen in Lafia on Tuesday.

Balarabe’s call followed the recent defection of the immediate past Chairman of Toto Local Government Area, Aliyu Abdullahi, from the APC.

The News Agency of Nigeria recalls that on September 14, the former chairman announced his resignation from the ruling APC.

The former speaker advocated for calm among APC members in Toto local government area.

Balarabe, who disagreed with the move by the former chairman, enjoined him to set aside whatever grievances and opt for dialogue, to resolve their differences amicably.

He also urged him to withdraw the resignation letter earlier issued and return to the APC.

“You cannot leave the house you have built for another person to inherit.

“APC is our home, it is our party, and our victory is assured by the will of Allah. We will get there. We will deliver our LGA In-Sha-Allah, come 2027.

“We cannot fold our hands and watch our party lose its members. We cannot fold our hands and allow our people to leave.

“In politics, everyone matters. The grassroots matter because politics is local, this is a fact,” Balarabe said.

The former speaker observed that success of APC as a party in the area come 2027, solidly depends on the unity and peace among the party members in the area.

“Unity of purpose is paramount for the task ahead of us, and no matter what, we must unite our people to facilitate victory in 2027,” he added.

World.title: NAF takes delivery of five new helicopters
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has taken delivery of five new helicopters as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to modernise and re-equip the Armed Forces to confront evolving security threats.

The newly acquired platforms comprise three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters manufactured by Leonardo Helicopters of Italy and two H-125 helicopters produced by Airbus Helicopters.

A statement by the NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said the acquisition was part of the Federal Government’s sustained investment in strengthening the operational capabilities of the service.

Ejodame said the three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters arrived in Lagos on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, as part of a batch of 10 recently acquired by the Federal Government.

He said the remaining seven helicopters were expected to be delivered before the end of 2026.

The two H-125 helicopters had earlier been delivered to the NAF, bringing the total number of helicopters covered by the latest acquisition to five.

Reacting to the development, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, described the acquisition as another milestone in the Federal Government’s ongoing investment in the modernisation and re-equipment of the NAF.

Aneke said the arrival of the helicopters would increase aircraft availability and give commanders greater flexibility in deploying airpower in support of ongoing military operations across the country.

According to him, the new platforms would particularly strengthen the NAF’s ability to provide timely air support to ground troops operating in challenging environments.

“The arrival of these five helicopters provides greater flexibility in the employment of airpower in support of ground troops in ongoing operations,” he said.

The Air Chief expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his continued support for the transformation and modernisation of the NAF.

Aneke said the Federal Government’s investment was enabling the service to progressively develop the capabilities required to meet its operational responsibilities and respond to Nigeria’s evolving security challenges.

He said the three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters would significantly boost the NAF’s rotary-wing capabilities.

He added that the platforms would enhance the service’s capacity for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), close air support, armed escort and combat search and rescue, as well as other joint missions in support of ground forces.

“The versatility of the AW-109 platform is expected to provide commanders with additional options for rapidly deploying air assets in support of troops engaged in counter-terrorism, counter-insurgency and other internal security operations,” Aneke said.

He said the helicopters would also improve the NAF’s ability to respond to emerging threats, particularly where speed, mobility and sustained aerial support were critical to ground operations.

According to him, the two H-125 helicopters would complement the AW-109s by providing versatile light-helicopter capabilities for various operational requirements.

The NAF said the platforms would collectively expand its flexibility and capacity to respond to changing operational demands, including moving personnel and equipment, conducting surveillance and supporting joint forces operating in difficult-to-reach areas.

Helicopters Undergoing Assembly

The NAF said the newly delivered platforms were undergoing post-delivery assembly and other technical processes ahead of their formal induction and operational deployment.

The process, it added, would include crew-readiness and technical preparations required to ensure that the helicopters were fully prepared for operational employment.

Aneke stressed that the NAF’s responsibility went beyond acquiring new platforms, noting that the service must ensure that the Federal Government’s investment translated into measurable operational results.

He said the service would continue to prioritise effective employment, maintenance and logistics sustainment to ensure maximum availability of the aircraft.

“We will continue to prioritise effective employment, maintenance and logistics sustainment so that every aircraft delivered adds measurable value to ongoing operations and the protection of the lives and property of Nigerians,” he said.

The acquisition comes as the Armed Forces continue operations against terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security threats across multiple theatres.

The NAF said the additional rotary-wing capacity would strengthen support for joint forces by improving the speed, reach and effectiveness of air support available to troops on the ground.

The new helicopters are expected to enhance operational mobility, surveillance and responsiveness while supporting ground forces in their efforts to counter terrorists and other criminal elements.

With the remaining seven AW-109 Trekker B helicopters expected before the end of 2026, the NAF is set to further expand its rotary-wing fleet and strengthen its capacity to provide air support for joint military operations.

World.title: ‘They are politically lazy’ – Wike tackles APC govs over Rainbow Coalition pushback
World.content:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has described governors of the All Progressives Congress as “politically lazy” following their opposition to his Rainbow Coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The governors, led by their chairman and Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, had said they would not participate in, support or endorse any alliance that could undermine President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid or affect APC candidates at any level.

But Wike, in an interview on Arise TV’s Prime Time on Tuesday, dismissed the concerns, arguing that his decision to support Tinubu did not mean he had abandoned his political party or agreed that other parties should not field candidates.

“They are politically lazy. When you have your local problems, don’t use Mr President as your excuse,” Wike said.

The minister maintained that the disagreements surrounding his political activities did not start with his decision to support Tinubu, recalling that he had faced opposition even when he was serving as governor of Rivers State and later as FCT minister.

“This thing did not start today. It started at ministerial position. They were not happy that I was Minister of FCT. Also, they were unhappy when I was governor,” he said.

Wike said his knowledge of the political situation was greater than that of those criticising his activities, suggesting that his critics would understand his position better if they had access to the information available to him.

“If they know what I know, they would not come out to shout,” he said.

The former Rivers State governor also insisted that his support for Tinubu remained unchanged, arguing that supporting the President was separate from the activities of his political party.

“I have said I will support the President and I am still supporting him. What has that got to do with my party?” Wike asked.

The minister further cited the political activities of governors such as Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo, Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke and Abia State Governor Alex Otti to argue that support for a presidential candidate should not prevent political parties from presenting candidates at other levels.

“Take Soludo, Adeleke and Otti. Does it mean that their parties will not present other candidates? This thing they are saying does not have any basis,” he said.

Wike also recalled the 2023 presidential election, saying his decision to support Tinubu was based on his belief that it was the South’s turn to produce the President after the Muhammadu Buhari administration.

“Recall that in 2023, as far as the President is concerned, it is my belief that it was the time of the South and so it would be unfair that it goes back to the North,” he said.
